facts.valueHtml: Cathedral + old town, then drive or train to Soller

facts.label: Rule
facts.valueHtml: Do not overfill this day before the beach-base transfer

days.note: This is the Mallorca variety day: one Gothic city block and one Tramuntana mountain-port block. The old train is charming but expensive for four, so treat it as optional.

spots.name: Palma old town + La Seu Cathedral
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · palmaIG · laseuIG · palmademallorcaFlickr

images.alt: Palma Cathedral and Royal Palace La Almudaina.
La Seu Cathedral in Palma de Mallorca.
Palma Cathedral in warm Mediterranean light.

spots.cost: Palma old town and Parc de la Mar are free. Cathedral baseline visit is roughly EUR10 adult, with children 9 and under free; terraces are a bigger EUR25 adult buy-up and not for under-9s, so the 8-year-old skips that version.
spots.climate: Mid-June Palma: warm, dry, and usually upper 70s to low 80s F. City stone gets hot after lunch, so do cathedral/old town early and move to a hotel pool or Cala Major/Portixol if the kids fade.
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip the terrace ticket with the 8-year-old; the outside, Parc de la Mar, old lanes, gelato, and a simple cathedral interior ticket are the better family value.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge One polished tapas dinner in Palma works here because the next four nights are beach-apartment simple.
spots.restoHtml:
• Family-restaurant shortlist — current Palma family lists surface pizza, Italian, and casual Mediterranean options
  • Can Joan de s Aigo — ensaimada, ice cream, hot chocolate; ideal picky-kid fallback
  • Pizza fallback — Palma has multiple easy pizzerias if tapas fails
spots.altboxHtml:
• Bellver Castle if the kids need ramparts instead of shopping streets.
  • Portixol waterfront for bikes/scooters and a calmer dinner walk.
  • Cala Major for a first Mallorca swim if the hotel pool is not enough.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Cathedral ticketsPalma with kids

spots.name: Port de Soller + Tramuntana villages
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · sollerIG · portdesollerIG · tramuntanaFlickr

images.alt: Wide view of Port de Soller and its curved bay.
Historic tram in Port de Soller.
Aerial view of Playa de Muro and Alcudia Bay.

spots.cost: Historic Soller train official fare signal: Palma-Soller return EUR30, or Palma-Port de Soller train+tram EUR40. For four, that is EUR120-EUR160 before lunch, so this is the optional splurge unless the kids love trains.
spots.climate: Tramuntana: cooler than Palma in the morning, hot by the port after lunch. Roads are gorgeous but narrow; motion-sick kids do better with fewer village stops.
spots.saveHtml: Save Drive the loop instead of paying the full train+tram stack; park once in Soller or Port de Soller and keep the day short.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Do the wooden train/tram combo once if the transportation itself is the attraction; it is expensive but memorable and eliminates mountain-road driving for the day.
spots.restoHtml:
• Port de Soller promenade — pizza, grilled fish, ice cream, and fries all within one waterfront walk
  • Soller market snacks — oranges, pastries, and simple sandwiches keep the train day flexible
spots.altboxHtml:
• Valldemossa only if the kids are done after one mountain village.
  • Deia viewpoint stop without the parking battle in the village core.
  • Hotel/pool afternoon if Tramuntana roads are slow or hot.

spots.cost: Beach is free; budget EUR25-EUR45/day for two loungers + umbrella when shade matters. Apartment-first lodging near Playa de Muro/Port d Alcudia is the budget gate: target $225-$300/night, walk away above ~$325/night.
spots.climate: Sea: Mallorca is usually about 72-75 F by mid/late June around Palma and the bays. Playa de Muro/Alcudia are shallow, sandy, and family-friendly, so this is the swim act Madeira cannot provide.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use a grocery breakfast, beach picnic, and apartment laundry. Four low-drama beach nights are cheaper than a full resort if you keep the lodging gate.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge One beach-club shade day or short bay boat trip is worth it if heat spikes or the 8-year-old needs an easier win.
spots.restoHtml:
• Port d Alcudia pizza list — Pizza Stellata / Don Vito style fallback if seafood loses
  • Alcudia family restaurants — Indian, tapas, burgers, and beach menus within a short drive
spots.altboxHtml:
• Hidropark Alcudia as the heat-wave rescue day, not a default spend.
  • S Albufera boardwalk for a cheap nature hour near the beach.
  • Alcudia old town walls at golden hour when the beach wind picks up.

spots.name: Plaka & Anafiotika
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · plakaIG · anafiotikaIG · athensFlickr

images.alt: Leafy taverna-lined lane climbing through Athens' Plaka quarter
Monastiraki square below the Acropolis, crowds and neoclassical facades
The Acropolis glowing at golden hour above the pine-covered Philopappou hill

spots.cost: Free to wander. Plaka is the old pedestrian quarter under the Acropolis — neoclassical lanes, tavernas, and souvenir stalls — and tucked into its upper slope is Anafiotika, a pocket of whitewashed, blue-doored Cycladic houses built by island masons in the 1840s. It is the trip’s gentle first taste of the islands, and a perfect jet-lag evening stroll.
spots.climate: Shaded, walkable, warm-evening. The narrow lanes hold shade even midday, and June evenings stay pleasant into the night. Anafiotika is residential — steep little stair-paths, worth the quiet respect (people live there).
spots.saveHtml: Save Make Plaka your free arrival-evening walk: climb the Anafiotika stairs for the rooftop-to-Lycabettus view at golden hour and eat where the locals do, off the main tourist strip.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A sit-down dinner on a vine-shaded Plaka terrace, plus a loukoumades (honey-doughnut) stop the kids will remember longer than any ruin.
spots.restoHtml:
• Plaka tavernas off the main lane — gyros, souvlaki, chips, and bread; the easiest picky-kid dinner in Athens
  • A Monastiraki pita counter — €3–4 pork/chicken gyros for a fast, cheap arrival-night meal
  • Loukoumades shop — hot honey doughnuts for dessert as the jet-lag treat
spots.altboxHtml:
• Anafiotika at golden hour for the whitewashed-village preview and the best rooftop light.
  • National Garden for a shaded, free morning with the 8-year-old before the Acropolis.
  • Panathenaic (Kallimarmaro) Stadium for a quick run around the marble track.

days.heading: The Acropolis
days.feel: The Parthenon, then the Acropolis Museum

facts.label: Heat rule
facts.valueHtml: Go at 8am open or after 6pm - midday is brutal

days.note: The one big culture day: the Acropolis at opening or late afternoon to beat the June heat, with the air-conditioned Acropolis Museum as the kid-friendly companion. Book the timed-entry slot in advance. Repack tonight for tomorrow’s ferry.

spots.name: The Acropolis & the marble city
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · acropolisIG · parthenonIG · athensFlickr

images.alt: Parthenon marble columns rising against a deep blue sky
The full Acropolis citadel on its rock above the treeline of Athens
The Caryatid porch of the Erechtheion on the Acropolis

spots.cost: The headline is the Acropolis: a combined site ticket is about €30 adult in summer; children under 5 are free and non-EU kids 6–25 pay a reduced ~€15, so a family of four runs roughly €75–90 (~$85–100). Since 2024 entry is a mandatory timed slot — book online at hhticket.gr and arrive in your 15-minute window. The separate Acropolis Museum is ~€15 (summer) and is the air-conditioned, kid-friendly companion.
spots.climate: Hot, dry, sunny inland. June highs average ~30°C / 86°F and there is almost no shade on the rock. Go at opening (~8am) or after 6pm; the midday climb is brutal for an 8-year-old. Carry 2+ liters of water, hats, and sunscreen; sunset is ~9pm, so a late-afternoon visit stays comfortable.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the earliest timed slot to beat the heat and the cruise crowds, and skip the paid guided tours — the free hilltop climb to Areopagus or Filopappou gives the postcard Parthenon view for nothing.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pair the site with the Acropolis Museum (the AC and the scale models are a genuine kid win), then a rooftop dinner in Plaka or Monastiraki with the lit Parthenon overhead.
spots.restoHtml:
• Tzitzikas kai Mermigas (Syntagma) — big Greek menu, famous fresh chips and grilled-pork pita the kids reliably eat
  • A Plaka pizza/pasta trattoria — wood-fired pizza and simple pasta a two-minute walk from the site for the pickiest eater
  • A family taverna at the foot of the Acropolis — pork or chicken gyros, tzatziki, bread, and fries as the dependable fallback
spots.altboxHtml:
• Late-afternoon Acropolis instead of morning if you want the marble in warm light and cooler air.
  • Acropolis Museum first on a scorching day for the AC, then the rock at 6pm.
  • Cape Sounion (Temple of Poseidon) as a half-day sea-cliff sunset drive if you have a spare afternoon.

days.heading: Ferry to Naxos, Portara sunset

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Sunset through the marble Portara your first evening

days.note: Morning high-speed ferry from Piraeus out to Naxos, the greenest and most kid-friendly Cyclade. Collect the rental car, settle into Chora, and walk out to the Portara for sunset — the great marble doorway framing the sun over the Aegean.

spots.name: Naxos Chora & the Portara at sunset
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · portaraIG · naxosIG · naxoschoraFlickr

images.alt: Sun bursting through the marble Portara gateway on Naxos at sunset
The Portara standing on its islet linked to Naxos Chora by a causeway
Naxos Chora and its harbour lit up at dusk seen from the water

spots.cost: Free, 24/7. The Portara — the colossal marble doorway of an unfinished 6th-century-BC Temple of Apollo — stands on the islet off Naxos Town, a 10-minute walk across the causeway and up ~75 steps. It frames the sunset like nothing else in the Cyclades. Below it, Naxos Chora tumbles up to a Venetian kastro of stone lanes.
spots.climate: Warm, sunny, breezy. June air tops out around ~28°C / 82°F with low humidity, and the sea has warmed to ~22°C / 72°F. Afternoons can pick up a north breeze (the meltemi is mild in early/mid June); the causeway to the Portara is exposed and glorious at golden hour.
spots.saveHtml: Save The Portara is free — make it your first-evening ritual, arriving 45 minutes before sunset for a spot on the marble. Wander the kastro lanes for nothing rather than paying for a walking tour.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A waterfront-taverna dinner in Chora after the sunset, then a Naxos kitron (citron) liqueur nightcap for the grown-ups.
spots.restoHtml:
• Caya (Naxos Town) — Italian-Mediterranean with wood-fired pizza and gnocchi, an easy picky-kid win
  • Scirocco (Protodikeiou Sq.) — family-run since 1995, modern Greek with pasta and grilled plates
  • Trata (Agios Georgios beach) — classic beach taverna: grilled meat, fries, pasta, calamari
spots.altboxHtml:
• Portara at dawn if you want it crowd-free instead of the sunset scrum.
  • Kastro walk + Della Rocca-Barozzi tower for a bit of Venetian history in the lanes.
  • Naxos Town harbor stroll for a low-key first evening if the flight day was long.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Portara — visiting infoNaxos in June — climate

days.travelNote: Travel day - Piraeus to Naxos by ferry.

days.heading: Naxos beach day

facts.label: Water
facts.valueHtml: Sea ~22°C / 72°F - the warmest, easiest swim of the trip

days.note: The reason Naxos is the base: long crescents of golden sand and gentle shallow water at Agios Prokopios and Plaka — the best family swimming on the trip. Swim in the calm morning, and keep the south beaches in your pocket if the afternoon breeze picks up.

spots.name: Agios Prokopios & Plaka: the long sandy beaches
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · agiosprokopiosIG · plakabeachIG · naxosFlickr

images.alt: The long sweep of sand at Plaka beach on Naxos meeting a calm sea
A turquoise Naxos bay backed by a whitewashed village and headland
A sheltered sandy cove with clear turquoise shallows on Naxos

spots.cost: The reason Naxos is the family base. Agios Prokopios is a Blue-Flag, 1.5 km crescent of golden sand with a gentle shallow shelf — the most kid-friendly swim on the trip. Sunbed-and-umbrella pairs run ~€20/day at the organized south end; the north end is free. Plaka beach next door is a 4 km ribbon of white sand and dunes. Water is a warming ~22°C / 72°F.
spots.climate: Sandy, shallow, west-facing. Warm sun and calm mornings; the meltemi, when it blows, hits these west-coast beaches strongest in the afternoon, so swim early and picnic late. For a truly wind-sheltered day, the south/east beaches (Agiassos, Kalantos) stay calmer.
spots.saveHtml: Save Park at the free north end of Agios Prokopios, bring your own umbrella, and swim before the afternoon breeze; a local bus (~€3.50) reaches the beaches if you skip the car that day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A front-row sunbed set with a beach-bar lunch, or a lesson at a Plaka/Mikri Vigla watersports center for the 13-year-old (windsurf/SUP).
spots.restoHtml:
• Beach-bar tavernas at Agios Prokopios — toasties, fries, pasta, and grilled fish steps from the sand
  • Caya or a Chora pizzeria — back in town for a reliable wood-fired-pizza dinner
  • Naxos Town gyros counters — cheap, fast picky-kid lunches between swims
spots.altboxHtml:
• Plaka beach dunes for a wilder, quieter stretch than Agios Prokopios.
  • Mikri Vigla for the windier watersports end if the teen wants a lesson.
  • Agiassos or Kalantos (south) as the meltemi-sheltered backup on a windy day.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Agios Prokopios guideNaxos June sea temperature

days.heading: Naxos mountain villages
days.daycost: Est. $130 · car day, tastings, taverna lunch

facts.label: Why
facts.valueHtml: Cooler, greener inland - a break from beach heat

days.note: Naxos is the one Cyclade with a real mountainous interior. Drive up through the Tragea olive valleys to Halki for a free citron-liqueur tasting, then marble-paved Apeiranthos — a cooler, greener half-day and a genuine change of pace from the sand.

spots.name: Halki & Apeiranthos: the mountain villages
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · apeiranthosIG · halkiIG · naxosFlickr

images.alt: A stone mountain village on Naxos looking out over the Aegean
A whitewashed Naxos hill village stepping down toward the sea
A bougainvillea-shaded taverna courtyard in a Naxos village

spots.cost: Naxos is the greenest, most mountainous Cyclade, and its inland villages are the antidote to a pure beach trip. Halki (~25 min up) is the old kitron capital: the free Vallindras distillery pours a family-friendly citron-liqueur tasting with a small museum. Apeiranthos (~30–40 min) is a marble-paved mountain village of Venetian towers and little museums. Both are free to wander; you just need the rental car and a couple of euros for coffee.
spots.climate: Cooler and greener up high. The drive climbs through Tragea olive valleys to villages several degrees cooler than the coast — a smart midday escape from beach heat or an afternoon meltemi. Marble lanes are shaded; bring grippy shoes for the cobbles.
spots.saveHtml: Save The villages cost nothing to explore and the Vallindras kitron tasting is free — make it a self-drive loop (Halki → Filoti → Apeiranthos) with a taverna lunch, no tour needed.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch at a mountain taverna in Apeiranthos or Filoti with a view over the Tragea, plus a stop at the Fish & Olive ceramics gallery in Halki.
spots.restoHtml:
• Apeiranthos / Filoti mountain tavernas — grilled meat, fries, and local cheese with a valley view
  • Halki cafes on the square — toasties, sweets, and drinks around the kitron distillery
  • A bakery in Chalki or Filoti — cheese pies and pastries for a picky-kid car lunch
spots.altboxHtml:
• Temple of Demeter (Sangri) as an easy ancient-site add-on on the way up.
  • Melanes / Flerio kouros to hunt the giant unfinished marble statue lying in an orchard.
  • Mount Zas cave for a short hike with the teen if you want a leg-stretch.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Halki (kitron village) guideNaxos villages one-day drive

days.heading: Naxos flex + Portara

facts.label: Flex
facts.valueHtml: Wind-led: sheltered beach, Chora kastro, or watersports

days.note: A flex day — read the wind and choose: another shallow-beach morning, the Venetian kastro lanes of Chora, or a watersports lesson at breezy Mikri Vigla for the teen. A relaxed last Naxos evening before the island-hop resumes. Repack tonight.

days.heading: Ferry to Paros, Naoussa

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Naoussa fishing harbor at golden hour

days.note: The easiest transfer of the trip: a 30–40 minute ferry hop to Paros. Base in or near Naoussa, the Cyclades’ loveliest fishing village — a working harbor, a half-sunk Venetian fort, and lanes that glow at sunset.

spots.name: Naoussa: the fishing harbor at golden hour
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · naoussaIG · parosIG · naoussaparosFlickr

images.alt: A traditional wooden boat in Naoussa harbour on Paros at sunset
The pier and white village of Naoussa reaching into a turquoise bay
Fishing boats moored along the breakwater rocks at Naoussa

spots.cost: Free to soak up. Naoussa is the prettiest fishing village in the Cyclades: a working harbor of caiques and octopus drying on the quay, a half-sunk 15th-century Venetian kastro you can wade to, and a warren of white lanes that fill with tavernas at night. Golden hour (~18:30–19:30 in June) lights the boats and the fort — the trip’s most romantic evening, and it costs nothing but dinner.
spots.climate: Warm, bright, breezy. June air ~28°C / 82°F, sea ~22°C / 72°F. Paros is a windsurf island for a reason — the afternoon meltemi is real here — but Naoussa’s harbor and lanes are sheltered and calm at dusk.
spots.saveHtml: Save Wander the harbor and kastro for free, wade out to the ruined fort, and eat gyros on the quay rather than a full sit-down if the budget is tight.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A seafood dinner on the Naoussa waterfront at sunset, then a gelato walk through the lantern-lit back lanes.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pita Frank (Naoussa) — legendary ~€3.50 gyros, customizable, an instant kid favorite
  • Taverna Glafkos (Naoussa) — family-run, pasta and traditional plates on the water
  • Cuore Rosso (Parikia) — widely rated the island’s best pizza for the pickiest eater
spots.altboxHtml:
• Parikia old town + Panagia Ekatontapyliani (the 4th-century "church of 100 doors") for a quieter afternoon.
  • Lefkes mountain village for a stone-lane, bougainvillea half-day inland.
  • Naoussa kastro swim off the rocks by the harbor fort.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Naoussa, Paros guideParos in June — weather

days.travelNote: Travel day - Naxos to Paros by ferry.

days.heading: Ferry to Milos, Plaka sunset

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Klima syrmata + Plaka castle at sunset

days.note: Ferry southwest to Milos, the volcanic showpiece. Collect the car, settle in Adamas or Pollonia, and ease in with the island’s villages: the color-doored syrmata of Klima and a sunset climb to the castle above whitewashed Plaka.

spots.name: Plaka, Klima & the fishing coves
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · klimaIG · plakamilosIG · firopotamosFlickr

images.alt: The colourful syrmata boathouses of Klima reflected in calm Milos water
Fishing boats and painted boathouses in the Mandrakia cove on Milos
A white chapel and Greek flag above the fishing coves of Milos

spots.cost: The island’s village-and-cove side. Klima is a row of syrmata — two-level fishermen’s houses with brightly painted doors carved right into the rock at the waterline, glowing at sunset. Hilltop Plaka is the whitewashed capital, with a free 200-step climb to a Venetian castle for one of the Aegean’s best sunsets. Firopotamos and Papafragas are tiny, photogenic swim coves. All free; you just need the car.
spots.climate: Warm evenings, west-facing sunsets. Klima and the Plaka castle both face west for the sunset; June nights are balmy for a village dinner. Papafragas has a steep, rocky final descent to the water — sturdy shoes, and mind the little ones.
spots.saveHtml: Save Klima, Plaka, and the castle are all free — make a sunset loop of them, park once and walk, and swim at Firopotamos rather than a paid beach.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Sunset dinner in Plaka after the castle climb, or a couple of nights based in pretty Pollonia at the quieter north end.
spots.restoHtml:
• Plaka / Trypiti tavernas — grilled plates and pasta with the sunset view
  • Adamas: Egoist & Gyros of Milos — burgers, pasta, and gyros for the picky crew
  • Pollonia seafront — relaxed pizza-and-seafood dinners at the north end
spots.altboxHtml:
• Plaka castle at sunset for the island’s cinematic view (200 steps up).
  • Mandrakia — another photogenic syrmata fishing hamlet if Klima is busy.
  • Firopotamos swim as the calm, sandy-ish north-coast cove.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Klima travel guideMilos best sunset spots

days.heading: Chania old town and town beaches
days.daycost: Est. $160-$280 - beach snacks, parking/taxi, casual dinner
days.note: Do not rush to the far west on the first full Crete day. After four hiking days and two flight days, this easy 73-degree swim day is what makes the whole two-island structure feel worth it.

spots.name: Chania old town + Nea Chora / Agii Apostoli
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ChaniaIG · Nea ChoraIG · Agii ApostoliFlickr

images.alt: The dramatic turquoise fjord-cove of Seitan Limania between steep cliffs
Aerial straight down the narrow Seitan Limania inlet to the turquoise water
A visitor on the pebble beach facing the narrow Seitan Limania cove

spots.cost: Harbor wandering and town beaches are free. Add $60-$150 family for chairs, gelato, simple dinner, and taxis/parking depending where you stay.
spots.climate: June: Chania averages around 84 F highs / 66 F lows; sea water around 73 F is the payoff the whole route is built around.
spots.saveHtml: Save Make arrival and recovery days mostly free: harbor, beach, bakery breakfast, and a simple pizza/gyro dinner.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Use one harbor dinner or sunset boat if the flight day went smoothly; skip if the family just needs sleep.
spots.restoHtml:
• Oregano's — Agii Apostoli wood-fired pizza, fresh pasta, grilled meats, and Greek basics
  • Goody's Burger House — burgers, chicken burgers, fries, and junior menu fallback
  • Lithos Restaurant — beef burger with fries, grilled chicken, chicken/pork gyros, and skewers
spots.altboxHtml:

  • Marathi Beach ↗ — calmer Akrotiri swim day when wind makes Balos or Elafonissi rough.
  • Falasarna sunset ↗ — self-drive big beach with a sunset payoff if a boat day is not the mood.

days.heading: Balos boat from Kissamos

facts.label: Wind swap
facts.valueHtml: Trade days with Elafonissi if needed

days.note: With Chania squeezed to five nights there is no dedicated flex day anymore - Balos and Elafonissi are deliberately back-to-back so they can swap by wind forecast. Keep it public-boat/simple unless the budget is pricing unusually low.

spots.name: Balos Lagoon by Kissamos boat
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Balos LagoonFlickr

images.alt: Balos Lagoon's white sandbar curving to Gramvousa from the hilltop overlook
Shallow turquoise water over the white sandbar at Balos Lagoon
Traditional excursion boat on turquoise water en route to Balos

spots.cost: Current 2026 pre-Jul-15 Gramvousa/Balos boat pricing: EUR 40 ages 13+, EUR 24 ages 3-12, plus EUR 1 municipal fee for passengers over 13. Family baseline about EUR 147 before meals.
spots.climate: Mid-June: hot, bright, and exposed. Water should be comfortable enough for real swimming, but shade and wind are the deciding factors.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the public Kissamos boat and bring snacks/water. Driving the rough Balos road adds car-risk and a steep walk back up.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Private boat only if the total trip is pricing near the low end; it can be wonderful, but it is the easiest budget blowout.
spots.restoHtml:
• Oregano's — Agii Apostoli wood-fired pizza, fresh pasta, grilled meats, and Greek basics
  • Goody's Burger House — burgers, chicken burgers, fries, and junior menu fallback
  • Lithos Restaurant — beef burger with fries, grilled chicken, chicken/pork gyros, and skewers
spots.altboxHtml:
• Falasarna sunset beach ↩ — simpler self-drive beach day if wind, boat timing, or budget makes Balos unattractive.
  • Agii Apostoli beaches ↗ — short-drive coves near Chania with easier food and less commitment.
  • Marathi Beach ↗ — calmer Akrotiri swim day when west-coast wind is the issue.

days.heading: Elafonissi lagoon or Falasarna sunset
days.daycost: Est. $160-$320 - fuel, parking, loungers/meals if used
days.note: Pick by wind and energy: Elafonissi is the shallow pink-sand lagoon day; Falasarna is the simpler big-beach/sunset day. If Balos got blown out on the prior boat outing, this is its replacement slot and the lagoon becomes the backup.

spots.name: Elafonissi Lagoon or Falasarna sunset
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ElafonissiIG · FalasarnaFlickr

images.alt: Elafonissi's pink sand and turquoise lagoon framed by black volcanic rock
Pink sand curving into the shallow turquoise lagoon at Elafonissi
Aerial of Elafonissi's pink-white sandbars and turquoise shallows

spots.cost: Beach entry is free. Elafonissi close parking currently advertises EUR 5/day; Falasarna loungers/umbrellas often vary by row/operator, so budget $60-$180 family if using chairs and meals.
spots.climate: Mid-June: shallow lagoon water feels warmer than open beaches. Wind is the variable; keep Falasarna as the sunset backup.
spots.saveHtml: Save Bring towels, water shoes, and snacks; use paid chairs only if you are staying several hours.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pay for a well-located sunbed set and a low-effort beach lunch when heat is high.
spots.restoHtml:
• Oregano's — Agii Apostoli wood-fired pizza, fresh pasta, grilled meats, and Greek basics
  • Goody's Burger House — burgers, chicken burgers, fries, and junior menu fallback
  • Lithos Restaurant — beef burger with fries, grilled chicken, chicken/pork gyros, and skewers
spots.altboxHtml:
• Agii Apostoli beaches ↩ — short-drive fallback near Chania if the family is done with long road days.
  • Limnoupolis Water Park ↗ — straight kid-win backup for heat, wind, or hike fatigue.
  • Marathi Beach ↗ — calmer Akrotiri swim day when wind makes Balos or Elafonissi rough.

days.heading: Imbros Gorge and south-coast swim
days.daycost: Est. $170-$330 - entrance, return ride/taxi, meals, fuel

facts.label: Hike
facts.valueHtml: 8km Imbros village -> Komitades; easier than Samaria

days.note: Imbros stays the family-accessible gorge: shorter, shadier, no ferry, and a good gut-check before deciding whether Samaria is a full descent or lazy-way outing on a later hiking day.

spots.name: Imbros Gorge + south-coast swim
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ImbrosFlickr

images.alt: A hiker spanning the towering walls at the narrowest point of Imbros Gorge
Golden light in the tight rock passage of Imbros Gorge
Sheer canyon walls and greenery along the Imbros Gorge trail

spots.cost: Entrance is typically EUR 3-EUR 5 pp cash. If self-driving, start at Imbros village and arrange a Komitades-to-Imbros return taxi/minibus before you begin; shared rides are commonly about EUR 8 pp, or roughly EUR 25-35 for a small private taxi.
spots.climate: 8 km, 2.5-4 hrs: easier and shorter than Samaria, mostly downhill from Imbros village to Komitades with shade in the narrows. Still rocky underfoot, with no services inside the gorge; start early and carry water.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the self-drive pattern: park at Imbros, walk down to Komitades, then take the pre-arranged local taxi/minibus back to the car. No ferry is required, which is why this is the gentler family gorge.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a Chania transfer tour if you do not want to manage the car-return logistics; the hike itself stays the same but the day becomes simpler.
spots.restoHtml:
• Oregano's — Agii Apostoli wood-fired pizza, fresh pasta, grilled meats, and Greek basics
  • Goody's Burger House — burgers, chicken burgers, fries, and junior menu fallback
  • Lithos Restaurant — beef burger with fries, grilled chicken, chicken/pork gyros, and skewers
spots.altboxHtml:
• Samaria Gorge ↩ — the epic 16 km version if everyone is trail-tested and the heat forecast cooperates.
  • Frangokastello Beach ↗ — south-coast swim and castle views after the gorge or as a low-effort swap.
  • Limnoupolis Water Park ↗ — straight kid-win backup for heat, wind, or hike fatigue.

days.heading: Arrive Athens, Plaka evening

facts.label: Transfer
facts.valueHtml: ATH airport -> Plaka ~40 min by taxi/metro

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Check in, wander Plaka & Anafiotika, early dinner

days.note: Land in Athens, drop bags near Plaka, and let the first evening be gentle: the pedestrian lanes of Plaka and the whitewashed island-in-the-city pocket of Anafiotika are the perfect jet-lag stroll before the islands begin.

spots.name: Plaka & Anafiotika
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · plakaIG · anafiotikaIG · athensFlickr

images.alt: Leafy taverna-lined lane climbing through Athens' Plaka quarter
Monastiraki square below the Acropolis, crowds and neoclassical facades
The Acropolis glowing at golden hour above the pine-covered Philopappou hill

spots.cost: Free to wander. Plaka is the old pedestrian quarter under the Acropolis — neoclassical lanes, tavernas, and souvenir stalls — and tucked into its upper slope is Anafiotika, a pocket of whitewashed, blue-doored Cycladic houses built by island masons in the 1840s. It is the trip’s gentle first taste of the islands, and a perfect jet-lag evening stroll.
spots.climate: Shaded, walkable, warm-evening. The narrow lanes hold shade even midday, and June evenings stay pleasant into the night. Anafiotika is residential — steep little stair-paths, worth the quiet respect (people live there).
spots.saveHtml: Save Make Plaka your free arrival-evening walk: climb the Anafiotika stairs for the rooftop-to-Lycabettus view at golden hour and eat where the locals do, off the main tourist strip.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A sit-down dinner on a vine-shaded Plaka terrace, plus a loukoumades (honey-doughnut) stop the kids will remember longer than any ruin.
spots.restoHtml:
• Plaka tavernas off the main lane — gyros, souvlaki, chips, and bread; the easiest picky-kid dinner in Athens
  • A Monastiraki pita counter — €3–4 pork/chicken gyros for a fast, cheap arrival-night meal
  • Loukoumades shop — hot honey doughnuts for dessert as the jet-lag treat
spots.altboxHtml:
• Anafiotika at golden hour for the whitewashed-village preview and the best rooftop light.
  • National Garden for a shaded, free morning with the 8-year-old before the Acropolis.
  • Panathenaic (Kallimarmaro) Stadium for a quick run around the marble track.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Anafiotika neighborhood guideAthens in June — weather

days.heading: The Acropolis
days.feel: The Parthenon, then the Acropolis Museum

facts.label: Heat rule
facts.valueHtml: Go at 8am open or after 6pm - midday is brutal

days.note: The one big culture day: the Acropolis at opening or late afternoon to beat the June heat, with the air-conditioned Acropolis Museum as the kid-friendly companion. Book the timed-entry slot in advance. Repack tonight for tomorrow’s ferry.

spots.name: The Acropolis & the marble city
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · acropolisIG · parthenonIG · athensFlickr

images.alt: Parthenon marble columns rising against a deep blue sky
The full Acropolis citadel on its rock above the treeline of Athens
The Caryatid porch of the Erechtheion on the Acropolis

spots.cost: The headline is the Acropolis: a combined site ticket is about €30 adult in summer; children under 5 are free and non-EU kids 6–25 pay a reduced ~€15, so a family of four runs roughly €75–90 (~$85–100). Since 2024 entry is a mandatory timed slot — book online at hhticket.gr and arrive in your 15-minute window. The separate Acropolis Museum is ~€15 (summer) and is the air-conditioned, kid-friendly companion.
spots.climate: Hot, dry, sunny inland. June highs average ~30°C / 86°F and there is almost no shade on the rock. Go at opening (~8am) or after 6pm; the midday climb is brutal for an 8-year-old. Carry 2+ liters of water, hats, and sunscreen; sunset is ~9pm, so a late-afternoon visit stays comfortable.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the earliest timed slot to beat the heat and the cruise crowds, and skip the paid guided tours — the free hilltop climb to Areopagus or Filopappou gives the postcard Parthenon view for nothing.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pair the site with the Acropolis Museum (the AC and the scale models are a genuine kid win), then a rooftop dinner in Plaka or Monastiraki with the lit Parthenon overhead.
spots.restoHtml:
• Tzitzikas kai Mermigas (Syntagma) — big Greek menu, famous fresh chips and grilled-pork pita the kids reliably eat
  • A Plaka pizza/pasta trattoria — wood-fired pizza and simple pasta a two-minute walk from the site for the pickiest eater
  • A family taverna at the foot of the Acropolis — pork or chicken gyros, tzatziki, bread, and fries as the dependable fallback
spots.altboxHtml:
• Late-afternoon Acropolis instead of morning if you want the marble in warm light and cooler air.
  • Acropolis Museum first on a scorching day for the AC, then the rock at 6pm.
  • Cape Sounion (Temple of Poseidon) as a half-day sea-cliff sunset drive if you have a spare afternoon.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Acropolis timed tickets — hhticket.grAcropolis Museum — plan your visit

days.heading: Ferry to Naxos, Portara sunset

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Sunset through the marble Portara your first evening

days.note: Morning high-speed ferry from Piraeus out to Naxos, the greenest and most kid-friendly Cyclade. Collect the rental car, settle into Chora, and walk out to the Portara for sunset — the great marble doorway framing the sun over the Aegean.

spots.name: Naxos Chora & the Portara at sunset
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · portaraIG · naxosIG · naxoschoraFlickr

images.alt: Sun bursting through the marble Portara gateway on Naxos at sunset
The Portara standing on its islet linked to Naxos Chora by a causeway
Naxos Chora and its harbour lit up at dusk seen from the water

spots.cost: Free, 24/7. The Portara — the colossal marble doorway of an unfinished 6th-century-BC Temple of Apollo — stands on the islet off Naxos Town, a 10-minute walk across the causeway and up ~75 steps. It frames the sunset like nothing else in the Cyclades. Below it, Naxos Chora tumbles up to a Venetian kastro of stone lanes.
spots.climate: Warm, sunny, breezy. June air tops out around ~28°C / 82°F with low humidity, and the sea has warmed to ~22°C / 72°F. Afternoons can pick up a north breeze (the meltemi is mild in early/mid June); the causeway to the Portara is exposed and glorious at golden hour.
spots.saveHtml: Save The Portara is free — make it your first-evening ritual, arriving 45 minutes before sunset for a spot on the marble. Wander the kastro lanes for nothing rather than paying for a walking tour.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A waterfront-taverna dinner in Chora after the sunset, then a Naxos kitron (citron) liqueur nightcap for the grown-ups.
spots.restoHtml:
• Caya (Naxos Town) — Italian-Mediterranean with wood-fired pizza and gnocchi, an easy picky-kid win
  • Scirocco (Protodikeiou Sq.) — family-run since 1995, modern Greek with pasta and grilled plates
  • Trata (Agios Georgios beach) — classic beach taverna: grilled meat, fries, pasta, calamari
spots.altboxHtml:
• Portara at dawn if you want it crowd-free instead of the sunset scrum.
  • Kastro walk + Della Rocca-Barozzi tower for a bit of Venetian history in the lanes.
  • Naxos Town harbor stroll for a low-key first evening if the flight day was long.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Portara — visiting infoNaxos in June — climate

days.heading: Naxos beach day

facts.label: Water
facts.valueHtml: Sea ~22°C / 72°F - the warmest, easiest swim of the trip

days.note: The reason Naxos is the base: long crescents of golden sand and gentle shallow water at Agios Prokopios and Plaka — the best family swimming on the trip. Swim in the calm morning, and keep the south beaches in your pocket if the afternoon breeze picks up.

spots.name: Agios Prokopios & Plaka: the long sandy beaches
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · agiosprokopiosIG · plakabeachIG · naxosFlickr

images.alt: The long sweep of sand at Plaka beach on Naxos meeting a calm sea
A turquoise Naxos bay backed by a whitewashed village and headland
A sheltered sandy cove with clear turquoise shallows on Naxos

spots.cost: The reason Naxos is the family base. Agios Prokopios is a Blue-Flag, 1.5 km crescent of golden sand with a gentle shallow shelf — the most kid-friendly swim on the trip. Sunbed-and-umbrella pairs run ~€20/day at the organized south end; the north end is free. Plaka beach next door is a 4 km ribbon of white sand and dunes. Water is a warming ~22°C / 72°F.
spots.climate: Sandy, shallow, west-facing. Warm sun and calm mornings; the meltemi, when it blows, hits these west-coast beaches strongest in the afternoon, so swim early and picnic late. For a truly wind-sheltered day, the south/east beaches (Agiassos, Kalantos) stay calmer.
spots.saveHtml: Save Park at the free north end of Agios Prokopios, bring your own umbrella, and swim before the afternoon breeze; a local bus (~€3.50) reaches the beaches if you skip the car that day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A front-row sunbed set with a beach-bar lunch, or a lesson at a Plaka/Mikri Vigla watersports center for the 13-year-old (windsurf/SUP).
spots.restoHtml:
• Beach-bar tavernas at Agios Prokopios — toasties, fries, pasta, and grilled fish steps from the sand
  • Caya or a Chora pizzeria — back in town for a reliable wood-fired-pizza dinner
  • Naxos Town gyros counters — cheap, fast picky-kid lunches between swims
spots.altboxHtml:
• Plaka beach dunes for a wilder, quieter stretch than Agios Prokopios.
  • Mikri Vigla for the windier watersports end if the teen wants a lesson.
  • Agiassos or Kalantos (south) as the meltemi-sheltered backup on a windy day.

days.heading: Naxos mountain villages
days.daycost: Est. $130 · car day, tastings, taverna lunch

facts.label: Why
facts.valueHtml: Cooler, greener inland - a break from beach heat

days.note: Naxos is the one Cyclade with a real mountainous interior. Drive up through the Tragea olive valleys to Halki for a free citron-liqueur tasting, then marble-paved Apeiranthos — a cooler, greener half-day and a genuine change of pace from the sand.

spots.name: Halki & Apeiranthos: the mountain villages
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · apeiranthosIG · halkiIG · naxosFlickr

images.alt: A stone mountain village on Naxos looking out over the Aegean
A whitewashed Naxos hill village stepping down toward the sea
A bougainvillea-shaded taverna courtyard in a Naxos village

spots.cost: Naxos is the greenest, most mountainous Cyclade, and its inland villages are the antidote to a pure beach trip. Halki (~25 min up) is the old kitron capital: the free Vallindras distillery pours a family-friendly citron-liqueur tasting with a small museum. Apeiranthos (~30–40 min) is a marble-paved mountain village of Venetian towers and little museums. Both are free to wander; you just need the rental car and a couple of euros for coffee.
spots.climate: Cooler and greener up high. The drive climbs through Tragea olive valleys to villages several degrees cooler than the coast — a smart midday escape from beach heat or an afternoon meltemi. Marble lanes are shaded; bring grippy shoes for the cobbles.
spots.saveHtml: Save The villages cost nothing to explore and the Vallindras kitron tasting is free — make it a self-drive loop (Halki → Filoti → Apeiranthos) with a taverna lunch, no tour needed.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch at a mountain taverna in Apeiranthos or Filoti with a view over the Tragea, plus a stop at the Fish & Olive ceramics gallery in Halki.
spots.restoHtml:
• Apeiranthos / Filoti mountain tavernas — grilled meat, fries, and local cheese with a valley view
  • Halki cafes on the square — toasties, sweets, and drinks around the kitron distillery
  • A bakery in Chalki or Filoti — cheese pies and pastries for a picky-kid car lunch
spots.altboxHtml:
• Temple of Demeter (Sangri) as an easy ancient-site add-on on the way up.
  • Melanes / Flerio kouros to hunt the giant unfinished marble statue lying in an orchard.
  • Mount Zas cave for a short hike with the teen if you want a leg-stretch.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Halki (kitron village) guideNaxos villages one-day drive

facts.label: Flex

days.note: A flex day — read the wind and choose: another shallow-beach morning, the Venetian kastro lanes of Chora, or a watersports lesson at breezy Mikri Vigla for the teen. A relaxed last Naxos evening before the island-hop resumes. Repack tonight.

days.heading: Ferry to Paros, Naoussa

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Naoussa fishing harbor at golden hour

days.note: The easiest transfer of the trip: a 30–40 minute ferry hop to Paros. Base in or near Naoussa, the Cyclades’ loveliest fishing village — a working harbor, a half-sunk Venetian fort, and lanes that glow at sunset.

spots.name: Naoussa: the fishing harbor at golden hour
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · naoussaIG · parosIG · naoussaparosFlickr

images.alt: A traditional wooden boat in Naoussa harbour on Paros at sunset
The pier and white village of Naoussa reaching into a turquoise bay
Fishing boats moored along the breakwater rocks at Naoussa

spots.cost: Free to soak up. Naoussa is the prettiest fishing village in the Cyclades: a working harbor of caiques and octopus drying on the quay, a half-sunk 15th-century Venetian kastro you can wade to, and a warren of white lanes that fill with tavernas at night. Golden hour (~18:30–19:30 in June) lights the boats and the fort — the trip’s most romantic evening, and it costs nothing but dinner.
spots.climate: Warm, bright, breezy. June air ~28°C / 82°F, sea ~22°C / 72°F. Paros is a windsurf island for a reason — the afternoon meltemi is real here — but Naoussa’s harbor and lanes are sheltered and calm at dusk.
spots.saveHtml: Save Wander the harbor and kastro for free, wade out to the ruined fort, and eat gyros on the quay rather than a full sit-down if the budget is tight.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A seafood dinner on the Naoussa waterfront at sunset, then a gelato walk through the lantern-lit back lanes.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pita Frank (Naoussa) — legendary ~€3.50 gyros, customizable, an instant kid favorite
  • Taverna Glafkos (Naoussa) — family-run, pasta and traditional plates on the water
  • Cuore Rosso (Parikia) — widely rated the island’s best pizza for the pickiest eater
spots.altboxHtml:
• Parikia old town + Panagia Ekatontapyliani (the 4th-century "church of 100 doors") for a quieter afternoon.
  • Lefkes mountain village for a stone-lane, bougainvillea half-day inland.
  • Naoussa kastro swim off the rocks by the harbor fort.

days.heading: Ferry to Milos, Plaka sunset

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Klima syrmata + Plaka castle at sunset

days.note: Ferry southwest to Milos, the volcanic showpiece. Collect the car, settle in Adamas or Pollonia, and ease in with the island’s villages: the color-doored syrmata of Klima and a sunset climb to the castle above whitewashed Plaka.

spots.name: Plaka, Klima & the fishing coves
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · klimaIG · plakamilosIG · firopotamosFlickr

images.alt: The colourful syrmata boathouses of Klima reflected in calm Milos water
Fishing boats and painted boathouses in the Mandrakia cove on Milos
A white chapel and Greek flag above the fishing coves of Milos

spots.cost: The island’s village-and-cove side. Klima is a row of syrmata — two-level fishermen’s houses with brightly painted doors carved right into the rock at the waterline, glowing at sunset. Hilltop Plaka is the whitewashed capital, with a free 200-step climb to a Venetian castle for one of the Aegean’s best sunsets. Firopotamos and Papafragas are tiny, photogenic swim coves. All free; you just need the car.
spots.climate: Warm evenings, west-facing sunsets. Klima and the Plaka castle both face west for the sunset; June nights are balmy for a village dinner. Papafragas has a steep, rocky final descent to the water — sturdy shoes, and mind the little ones.
spots.saveHtml: Save Klima, Plaka, and the castle are all free — make a sunset loop of them, park once and walk, and swim at Firopotamos rather than a paid beach.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Sunset dinner in Plaka after the castle climb, or a couple of nights based in pretty Pollonia at the quieter north end.
spots.restoHtml:
• Plaka / Trypiti tavernas — grilled plates and pasta with the sunset view
  • Adamas: Egoist & Gyros of Milos — burgers, pasta, and gyros for the picky crew
  • Pollonia seafront — relaxed pizza-and-seafood dinners at the north end
spots.altboxHtml:
• Plaka castle at sunset for the island’s cinematic view (200 steps up).
  • Mandrakia — another photogenic syrmata fishing hamlet if Klima is busy.
  • Firopotamos swim as the calm, sandy-ish north-coast cove.

days.heading: Kleftiko boat day

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Full-day Kleftiko cruise (book early in the stay)

days.note: The marquee: a full-day boat to Kleftiko’s white sea caves and arches, with swim and snorkel stops along the roadless southwest coast. Keep it flexible — if the wind is up, this is the day that slides into the buffer.

spots.name: Kleftiko: the sea caves by boat
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · kleftikoIG · milosIG · kleftikomilosFlickr

images.alt: Aerial of Kleftiko's white sea stacks and yachts in turquoise water
A towering white sea arch rising from the water at Kleftiko
A small boat gliding into a white sea cave arch at Kleftiko

spots.cost: The trip’s marquee: Kleftiko — a cathedral of white volcanic sea caves, arches, and stacks on Milos’s roadless southwest coast — is reachable only by boat. A full-day group cruise from Adamas or Pollonia runs ~€120–175/person (kids often reduced) and typically includes several swim/snorkel stops, gear, and lunch on board; a family of four is roughly €400–620 (~$450–680). Operators include Horizon, Excellent Yachting, Polco Sailing, and Zephyros.
spots.climate: The wind-dependent day — the one to keep flexible. Kleftiko faces the open southwest, so a strong meltemi can force operators to cancel or reroute at short notice. June is the calm shoulder (the meltemi peaks in July–August), and cancellations are uncommon, but this is exactly why the plan carries buffer days: book it early in the Milos stay so a blown-out day can slide.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take a larger group boat rather than a private charter, book directly with a Milos operator, and pick a morning departure when the sea is calmest.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A small-group or semi-private sailing catamaran to Kleftiko with fewer people, more swim time, and a proper on-board lunch.
spots.restoHtml:
• Lunch is aboard — most full-day Kleftiko cruises feed you on the boat, so this is a packed day
  • Adamas waterfront on return — Aktaion for pizza/pasta or a gyros counter for the kids
  • Pollonia tavernas — if you sail from the north end, an easy seafood-or-pasta dinner after
spots.altboxHtml:
• Half-day Kleftiko motorboat tour if a full 9-hour day is too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Reschedule within the Milos stay if the wind is up — the built-in reason for three nights.
  • Papafragas + Sarakiniko by car as the no-boat backup if Kleftiko blows out entirely.

spots.cost: Lefkada’s west coast is a run of white-cliff, turquoise-water beaches. Porto Katsiki is the postcard — ~80–100 steps down from a paid clifftop lot (~€8–15/day, half-price after 4pm; no beach fee). Kathisma is the big, easy, organised beach (free lot, sunbeds, tavernas) — the family-friendly pick. Egremni is currently boat-only after a June 2025 municipal closure of the land route (re-verify for 2027); day boats reach it from Nydri/Vasiliki.
spots.climate: Go in the morning. These west-facing beaches are calm at dawn, but the NW Maistro builds from midday and brings real chop and bigger waves by afternoon — every source says visit early for calm water and a parking spot. Kathisma is the most sheltered and stroller-friendly; Porto Katsiki’s steep climb is hot at midday.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do Kathisma (free parking, sunbeds, easy access) as the main swim and Porto Katsiki as a morning photo-and-dip; skip paid sunbeds and bring shade.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A boat trip from Vasiliki/Nydri that reaches Porto Katsiki and boat-only Egremni from the water, avoiding the cliff stairs entirely.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rachi, Exanthia — famous sunset-view taverna above the west coast, simple options for kids
  • Kathisma beach bars — fries, toasties, and pasta right on the sand
  • Pack water + snacks — Porto Katsiki has only a small kantina
spots.altboxHtml:
• Kathisma over Porto Katsiki if the kids won’t do the cliff stairs.
  • Kavalikefta for a quieter, wilder west-coast cove (narrow access road).
  • Boat to Egremni/Porto Katsiki for the cliff beaches without the climb.

days.note: A change of pace: the pretty car-free village of Agios Nikitas and a water-taxi hop to Milos beach in the calm morning, then south to windsurf-famous Vasiliki bay where the older kid can try a beginner lesson on the reliable afternoon wind.

spots.name: Agios Nikitas village, Milos beach & Vasiliki bay
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · agiosnikitasIG · milosbeachIG · vasilikiFlickr

images.alt: Windsurfers skimming the breezy blue bay at Vasiliki, Lefkada
A turquoise Lefkada beach below a green headland

spots.cost: Agios Nikitas is Lefkada’s prettiest, car-free stone village — walkable lanes and easy tavernas. Just around the headland, Milos beach is reached on foot (15–20 min uphill each way, past an old windmill) or by a ~5-min water taxi (~€5–10pp) — the easier call with kids. Down south, Vasiliki bay is a windsurf mecca; the 13-year-old can try a beginner lesson on the reliable afternoon wind.
spots.climate: Village mornings, wind sports afternoons. Milos and the west side are calmest before midday; Vasiliki is the opposite — flat and calm early, then a dependable ~15–20kt thermal wind fills in around 3pm (which is exactly why windsurfers love it). Schedule family swims in the morning and any windsurf lesson for the afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk to Milos beach instead of the water taxi if the kids are up for the uphill return; wander Agios Nikitas and swim off the village beach for free.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A beginner windsurf lesson at Vasiliki for the older kid, and a sunset dinner in car-free Agios Nikitas.

days.heading: Meganisi boat day
days.feel: Sea caves, Skorpios & a shaded gorge

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Nydri boat: Papanikolis cave + Skorpios swim stop

facts.label: Option
facts.valueHtml: Dimosari gorge walk (low flow by June)

days.note: The Lefkada boat day from Nydri: motoring into the Papanikolis sea cave and around the old Onassis islands with turquoise swim stops — sheltered and gentle for the kids — with the shaded Dimosari gorge as a cool-off alternative if you want land time.

spots.name: Nydri: Meganisi boat day & the Dimosari gorge
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · nydriIG · meganisiIG · skorpiosFlickr

images.alt: Nydri's harbour and peninsula lit up at dusk from above
The Nydri waterfront and its moored boats below green hills
An aerial of Nydri's white town and boat-filled harbour

spots.cost: From Nydri harbour, a wooden day-boat cruises the Meganisi channel: the boat motors inside the Papanikolis sea cave (a real kid wow), then loops the former Onassis islands of Skorpios and Madouri with a turquoise swim stop — roughly €30–40pp for a group cruise, ~€70–80pp with lunch. Pair a morning gorge or afternoon boat: the free Dimosari gorge walk near Nydri is a short, shaded canyon (parking free), though the falls run low by June — treat it as a pretty walk, not a waterfall swim.
spots.climate: Calm channel, shaded gorge. The Meganisi/Skorpios cruise is sheltered and gentle — good for the 8-year-old — with warm ~73°F swim stops in turquoise coves. The Dimosari gorge is shaded and cool, a fine hot-afternoon alternative, but manage expectations on the waterfall flow by mid-June.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take the group wooden-boat cruise (not a private charter) and bring your own snacks; the Dimosari gorge and its trailhead parking are free.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A smaller-group Meganisi cruise with lunch and more swim stops, or a private boat to time the Papanikolis cave without crowds.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pomodoro, Nydri — wood-fired pizza and pasta on the marina, a picky-kid favourite
  • Nydri waterfront tavernas — grills and simple plates along the harbour
  • The Plane Tree, Dimosari trailhead — drinks/snacks at the gorge entrance
spots.altboxHtml:
• Boat only if the gorge is dry — the Meganisi cruise is the real highlight.
  • Dimosari gorge morning, boat afternoon, or vice versa.
  • Sivota bay lunch by boat or car for another turquoise cove.

days.feel: An easy last day and repack

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Lefkada Town, the causeway, the Gyra windmills

facts.label: Tonight

days.note: A relaxed finale: walkable Lefkada Town, the floating causeway, and the flat lagoon loop past the Gyra windmills, with a last waterfront dinner.

spots.name: Lefkada Town, the lagoon & Gyra windmills
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lefkadatownIG · gyraIG · lefkadaFlickr

images.alt: A flower-lined waterfront promenade with umbrellas in Lefkada town
Sailboat masts along Lefkada's calm marina channel and mountains
Rows of yachts moored in Lefkada marina below green mountains

spots.cost: An easy, free last day. Lefkada Town connects to the mainland by the Agia Mavra floating causeway (no ferry ever needed to reach the island), and its centre is walkable and full of casual tavernas. The flat ~7km Gyra loop path rings the western lagoon past the surviving stone windmills and Gyra beach — a relaxed bike or drive-and-stroll to close the trip and repack before the short hop to Preveza airport.
spots.climate: Warm, flat, and shadeless around the lagoon. Walk or cycle the Gyra loop early or late; midday on the exposed spit is hot. The town itself has shaded lanes and a swing bridge that opens on the hour for boats — an easy, low-key finale after a busy Lefkada week.
spots.saveHtml: Save The whole day is essentially free — walk the town, the lagoon path, and Gyra beach, and eat a final pizza in the centre.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A last seafood dinner on the Lefkada Town waterfront, or a sunset drink out at the Gyra windmills.
spots.restoHtml:
• Made in Love, Lefkada Town — Neapolitan-trained pizzeria, family-friendly, gluten-free dough option
  • Lefkada Town centre tavernas — simple pasta, grills, and gyros in the walkable lanes
  • Bakeries + gelato — easy trailside snacks for the lagoon loop
spots.altboxHtml:
• Gyra beach swim for one last dip near town.
  • Bike the lagoon loop instead of driving for an active last morning.
  • Early repack — Preveza airport is only ~20–36 min via the causeway.

days.heading: The Acropolis
days.feel: The Parthenon, then the Acropolis Museum

facts.label: Heat rule
facts.valueHtml: Go at 8am open or after 6pm - midday is brutal

days.note: The one big culture day: the Acropolis at opening or late afternoon to beat the June heat, with the air-conditioned Acropolis Museum as the kid-friendly companion. Book the timed-entry slot in advance. Repack tonight for tomorrow’s ferry.

spots.name: The Acropolis & the marble city
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · acropolisIG · parthenonIG · athensFlickr

images.alt: Parthenon marble columns rising against a deep blue sky
The full Acropolis citadel on its rock above the treeline of Athens
The Caryatid porch of the Erechtheion on the Acropolis

spots.cost: The headline is the Acropolis: a combined site ticket is about €30 adult in summer; children under 5 are free and non-EU kids 6–25 pay a reduced ~€15, so a family of four runs roughly €75–90 (~$85–100). Since 2024 entry is a mandatory timed slot — book online at hhticket.gr and arrive in your 15-minute window. The separate Acropolis Museum is ~€15 (summer) and is the air-conditioned, kid-friendly companion.
spots.climate: Hot, dry, sunny inland. June highs average ~30°C / 86°F and there is almost no shade on the rock. Go at opening (~8am) or after 6pm; the midday climb is brutal for an 8-year-old. Carry 2+ liters of water, hats, and sunscreen; sunset is ~9pm, so a late-afternoon visit stays comfortable.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the earliest timed slot to beat the heat and the cruise crowds, and skip the paid guided tours — the free hilltop climb to Areopagus or Filopappou gives the postcard Parthenon view for nothing.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pair the site with the Acropolis Museum (the AC and the scale models are a genuine kid win), then a rooftop dinner in Plaka or Monastiraki with the lit Parthenon overhead.
spots.restoHtml:
• Tzitzikas kai Mermigas (Syntagma) — big Greek menu, famous fresh chips and grilled-pork pita the kids reliably eat
  • A Plaka pizza/pasta trattoria — wood-fired pizza and simple pasta a two-minute walk from the site for the pickiest eater
  • A family taverna at the foot of the Acropolis — pork or chicken gyros, tzatziki, bread, and fries as the dependable fallback
spots.altboxHtml:
• Late-afternoon Acropolis instead of morning if you want the marble in warm light and cooler air.
  • Acropolis Museum first on a scorching day for the AC, then the rock at 6pm.
  • Cape Sounion (Temple of Poseidon) as a half-day sea-cliff sunset drive if you have a spare afternoon.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Acropolis timed tickets — hhticket.grAcropolis Museum — plan your visit

days.heading: Ferry to Naxos, Portara sunset

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Sunset through the marble Portara your first evening

days.note: Morning high-speed ferry from Piraeus out to Naxos, the greenest and most kid-friendly Cyclade. Collect the rental car, settle into Chora, and walk out to the Portara for sunset — the great marble doorway framing the sun over the Aegean.

spots.name: Naxos Chora & the Portara at sunset
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · portaraIG · naxosIG · naxoschoraFlickr

images.alt: Sun bursting through the marble Portara gateway on Naxos at sunset
The Portara standing on its islet linked to Naxos Chora by a causeway
Naxos Chora and its harbour lit up at dusk seen from the water

spots.cost: Free, 24/7. The Portara — the colossal marble doorway of an unfinished 6th-century-BC Temple of Apollo — stands on the islet off Naxos Town, a 10-minute walk across the causeway and up ~75 steps. It frames the sunset like nothing else in the Cyclades. Below it, Naxos Chora tumbles up to a Venetian kastro of stone lanes.
spots.climate: Warm, sunny, breezy. June air tops out around ~28°C / 82°F with low humidity, and the sea has warmed to ~22°C / 72°F. Afternoons can pick up a north breeze (the meltemi is mild in early/mid June); the causeway to the Portara is exposed and glorious at golden hour.
spots.saveHtml: Save The Portara is free — make it your first-evening ritual, arriving 45 minutes before sunset for a spot on the marble. Wander the kastro lanes for nothing rather than paying for a walking tour.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A waterfront-taverna dinner in Chora after the sunset, then a Naxos kitron (citron) liqueur nightcap for the grown-ups.
spots.restoHtml:
• Caya (Naxos Town) — Italian-Mediterranean with wood-fired pizza and gnocchi, an easy picky-kid win
  • Scirocco (Protodikeiou Sq.) — family-run since 1995, modern Greek with pasta and grilled plates
  • Trata (Agios Georgios beach) — classic beach taverna: grilled meat, fries, pasta, calamari
spots.altboxHtml:
• Portara at dawn if you want it crowd-free instead of the sunset scrum.
  • Kastro walk + Della Rocca-Barozzi tower for a bit of Venetian history in the lanes.
  • Naxos Town harbor stroll for a low-key first evening if the flight day was long.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Portara — visiting infoNaxos in June — climate

days.travelNote: Travel day - Piraeus to Naxos by ferry.

days.heading: Naxos beach day

facts.label: Water
facts.valueHtml: Sea ~22°C / 72°F - the warmest, easiest swim of the trip

days.note: The reason Naxos is the base: long crescents of golden sand and gentle shallow water at Agios Prokopios and Plaka — the best family swimming on the trip. Swim in the calm morning, and keep the south beaches in your pocket if the afternoon breeze picks up.

spots.name: Agios Prokopios & Plaka: the long sandy beaches
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · agiosprokopiosIG · plakabeachIG · naxosFlickr

images.alt: The long sweep of sand at Plaka beach on Naxos meeting a calm sea
A turquoise Naxos bay backed by a whitewashed village and headland
A sheltered sandy cove with clear turquoise shallows on Naxos

spots.cost: The reason Naxos is the family base. Agios Prokopios is a Blue-Flag, 1.5 km crescent of golden sand with a gentle shallow shelf — the most kid-friendly swim on the trip. Sunbed-and-umbrella pairs run ~€20/day at the organized south end; the north end is free. Plaka beach next door is a 4 km ribbon of white sand and dunes. Water is a warming ~22°C / 72°F.
spots.climate: Sandy, shallow, west-facing. Warm sun and calm mornings; the meltemi, when it blows, hits these west-coast beaches strongest in the afternoon, so swim early and picnic late. For a truly wind-sheltered day, the south/east beaches (Agiassos, Kalantos) stay calmer.
spots.saveHtml: Save Park at the free north end of Agios Prokopios, bring your own umbrella, and swim before the afternoon breeze; a local bus (~€3.50) reaches the beaches if you skip the car that day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A front-row sunbed set with a beach-bar lunch, or a lesson at a Plaka/Mikri Vigla watersports center for the 13-year-old (windsurf/SUP).
spots.restoHtml:
• Beach-bar tavernas at Agios Prokopios — toasties, fries, pasta, and grilled fish steps from the sand
  • Caya or a Chora pizzeria — back in town for a reliable wood-fired-pizza dinner
  • Naxos Town gyros counters — cheap, fast picky-kid lunches between swims
spots.altboxHtml:
• Plaka beach dunes for a wilder, quieter stretch than Agios Prokopios.
  • Mikri Vigla for the windier watersports end if the teen wants a lesson.
  • Agiassos or Kalantos (south) as the meltemi-sheltered backup on a windy day.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Agios Prokopios guideNaxos June sea temperature

days.heading: Naxos mountain villages
days.daycost: Est. $130 · car day, tastings, taverna lunch

facts.label: Why
facts.valueHtml: Cooler, greener inland - a break from beach heat

days.note: Naxos is the one Cyclade with a real mountainous interior. Drive up through the Tragea olive valleys to Halki for a free citron-liqueur tasting, then marble-paved Apeiranthos — a cooler, greener half-day and a genuine change of pace from the sand.

spots.name: Halki & Apeiranthos: the mountain villages
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · apeiranthosIG · halkiIG · naxosFlickr

images.alt: A stone mountain village on Naxos looking out over the Aegean
A whitewashed Naxos hill village stepping down toward the sea
A bougainvillea-shaded taverna courtyard in a Naxos village

spots.cost: Naxos is the greenest, most mountainous Cyclade, and its inland villages are the antidote to a pure beach trip. Halki (~25 min up) is the old kitron capital: the free Vallindras distillery pours a family-friendly citron-liqueur tasting with a small museum. Apeiranthos (~30–40 min) is a marble-paved mountain village of Venetian towers and little museums. Both are free to wander; you just need the rental car and a couple of euros for coffee.
spots.climate: Cooler and greener up high. The drive climbs through Tragea olive valleys to villages several degrees cooler than the coast — a smart midday escape from beach heat or an afternoon meltemi. Marble lanes are shaded; bring grippy shoes for the cobbles.
spots.saveHtml: Save The villages cost nothing to explore and the Vallindras kitron tasting is free — make it a self-drive loop (Halki → Filoti → Apeiranthos) with a taverna lunch, no tour needed.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch at a mountain taverna in Apeiranthos or Filoti with a view over the Tragea, plus a stop at the Fish & Olive ceramics gallery in Halki.
spots.restoHtml:
• Apeiranthos / Filoti mountain tavernas — grilled meat, fries, and local cheese with a valley view
  • Halki cafes on the square — toasties, sweets, and drinks around the kitron distillery
  • A bakery in Chalki or Filoti — cheese pies and pastries for a picky-kid car lunch
spots.altboxHtml:
• Temple of Demeter (Sangri) as an easy ancient-site add-on on the way up.
  • Melanes / Flerio kouros to hunt the giant unfinished marble statue lying in an orchard.
  • Mount Zas cave for a short hike with the teen if you want a leg-stretch.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Halki (kitron village) guideNaxos villages one-day drive

days.heading: Naxos flex + Portara

facts.label: Flex
facts.valueHtml: Wind-led: sheltered beach, Chora kastro, or watersports

days.note: A flex day — read the wind and choose: another shallow-beach morning, the Venetian kastro lanes of Chora, or a watersports lesson at breezy Mikri Vigla for the teen. A relaxed last Naxos evening before the island-hop resumes. Repack tonight.

days.heading: Ferry to Paros, Naoussa

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Naoussa fishing harbor at golden hour

days.note: The easiest transfer of the trip: a 30–40 minute ferry hop to Paros. Base in or near Naoussa, the Cyclades’ loveliest fishing village — a working harbor, a half-sunk Venetian fort, and lanes that glow at sunset.

spots.name: Naoussa: the fishing harbor at golden hour
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · naoussaIG · parosIG · naoussaparosFlickr

images.alt: A traditional wooden boat in Naoussa harbour on Paros at sunset
The pier and white village of Naoussa reaching into a turquoise bay
Fishing boats moored along the breakwater rocks at Naoussa

spots.cost: Free to soak up. Naoussa is the prettiest fishing village in the Cyclades: a working harbor of caiques and octopus drying on the quay, a half-sunk 15th-century Venetian kastro you can wade to, and a warren of white lanes that fill with tavernas at night. Golden hour (~18:30–19:30 in June) lights the boats and the fort — the trip’s most romantic evening, and it costs nothing but dinner.
spots.climate: Warm, bright, breezy. June air ~28°C / 82°F, sea ~22°C / 72°F. Paros is a windsurf island for a reason — the afternoon meltemi is real here — but Naoussa’s harbor and lanes are sheltered and calm at dusk.
spots.saveHtml: Save Wander the harbor and kastro for free, wade out to the ruined fort, and eat gyros on the quay rather than a full sit-down if the budget is tight.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A seafood dinner on the Naoussa waterfront at sunset, then a gelato walk through the lantern-lit back lanes.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pita Frank (Naoussa) — legendary ~€3.50 gyros, customizable, an instant kid favorite
  • Taverna Glafkos (Naoussa) — family-run, pasta and traditional plates on the water
  • Cuore Rosso (Parikia) — widely rated the island’s best pizza for the pickiest eater
spots.altboxHtml:
• Parikia old town + Panagia Ekatontapyliani (the 4th-century "church of 100 doors") for a quieter afternoon.
  • Lefkes mountain village for a stone-lane, bougainvillea half-day inland.

days.heading: Ferry to Milos, Plaka sunset

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Klima syrmata + Plaka castle at sunset

days.note: Ferry southwest to Milos, the volcanic showpiece. Collect the car, settle in Adamas or Pollonia, and ease in with the island’s villages: the color-doored syrmata of Klima and a sunset climb to the castle above whitewashed Plaka.

spots.name: Plaka, Klima & the fishing coves
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · klimaIG · plakamilosIG · firopotamosFlickr

images.alt: The colourful syrmata boathouses of Klima reflected in calm Milos water
Fishing boats and painted boathouses in the Mandrakia cove on Milos
A white chapel and Greek flag above the fishing coves of Milos

spots.cost: The island’s village-and-cove side. Klima is a row of syrmata — two-level fishermen’s houses with brightly painted doors carved right into the rock at the waterline, glowing at sunset. Hilltop Plaka is the whitewashed capital, with a free 200-step climb to a Venetian castle for one of the Aegean’s best sunsets. Firopotamos and Papafragas are tiny, photogenic swim coves. All free; you just need the car.
spots.climate: Warm evenings, west-facing sunsets. Klima and the Plaka castle both face west for the sunset; June nights are balmy for a village dinner. Papafragas has a steep, rocky final descent to the water — sturdy shoes, and mind the little ones.
spots.saveHtml: Save Klima, Plaka, and the castle are all free — make a sunset loop of them, park once and walk, and swim at Firopotamos rather than a paid beach.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Sunset dinner in Plaka after the castle climb, or a couple of nights based in pretty Pollonia at the quieter north end.
spots.restoHtml:
• Plaka / Trypiti tavernas — grilled plates and pasta with the sunset view
  • Adamas: Egoist & Gyros of Milos — burgers, pasta, and gyros for the picky crew
  • Pollonia seafront — relaxed pizza-and-seafood dinners at the north end
spots.altboxHtml:
• Plaka castle at sunset for the island’s cinematic view (200 steps up).
  • Mandrakia — another photogenic syrmata fishing hamlet if Klima is busy.
  • Firopotamos swim as the calm, sandy-ish north-coast cove.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Klima travel guideMilos best sunset spots

days.heading: Kleftiko boat day

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Full-day Kleftiko cruise (book early in the stay)

days.note: The marquee: a full-day boat to Kleftiko’s white sea caves and arches, with swim and snorkel stops along the roadless southwest coast. Keep it flexible — if the wind is up, this is the day that slides into the buffer.

spots.name: Kleftiko: the sea caves by boat
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · kleftikoIG · milosIG · kleftikomilosFlickr

images.alt: Aerial of Kleftiko's white sea stacks and yachts in turquoise water
A towering white sea arch rising from the water at Kleftiko
A small boat gliding into a white sea cave arch at Kleftiko

spots.cost: The trip’s marquee: Kleftiko — a cathedral of white volcanic sea caves, arches, and stacks on Milos’s roadless southwest coast — is reachable only by boat. A full-day group cruise from Adamas or Pollonia runs ~€120–175/person (kids often reduced) and typically includes several swim/snorkel stops, gear, and lunch on board; a family of four is roughly €400–620 (~$450–680). Operators include Horizon, Excellent Yachting, Polco Sailing, and Zephyros.
spots.climate: The wind-dependent day — the one to keep flexible. Kleftiko faces the open southwest, so a strong meltemi can force operators to cancel or reroute at short notice. June is the calm shoulder (the meltemi peaks in July–August), and cancellations are uncommon, but this is exactly why the plan carries buffer days: book it early in the Milos stay so a blown-out day can slide.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take a larger group boat rather than a private charter, book directly with a Milos operator, and pick a morning departure when the sea is calmest.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A small-group or semi-private sailing catamaran to Kleftiko with fewer people, more swim time, and a proper on-board lunch.
spots.restoHtml:
• Lunch is aboard — most full-day Kleftiko cruises feed you on the boat, so this is a packed day
  • Adamas waterfront on return — Aktaion for pizza/pasta or a gyros counter for the kids
  • Pollonia tavernas — if you sail from the north end, an easy seafood-or-pasta dinner after
spots.altboxHtml:
• Half-day Kleftiko motorboat tour if a full 9-hour day is too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Reschedule within the Milos stay if the wind is up — the built-in reason for three nights.
  • Papafragas + Sarakiniko by car as the no-boat backup if Kleftiko blows out entirely.

facts.label: Hike
facts.valueHtml: 8km Imbros village -> Komitades; easier than Samaria

days.note: Imbros stays the family-accessible gorge: shorter, shadier, no ferry, and a good gut-check before deciding whether Samaria is a full descent or lazy-way outing on a later hiking day.

spots.name: Imbros Gorge + south-coast swim
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ImbrosFlickr

images.alt: A hiker spanning the towering walls at the narrowest point of Imbros Gorge
Golden light in the tight rock passage of Imbros Gorge

spots.cost: Entrance is typically EUR 3-EUR 5 pp cash. If self-driving, start at Imbros village and arrange a Komitades-to-Imbros return taxi/minibus before you begin; shared rides are commonly about EUR 8 pp, or roughly EUR 25-35 for a small private taxi.
spots.climate: 8 km, 2.5-4 hrs: easier and shorter than Samaria, mostly downhill from Imbros village to Komitades with shade in the narrows. Still rocky underfoot, with no services inside the gorge; start early and carry water.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the self-drive pattern: park at Imbros, walk down to Komitades, then take the pre-arranged local taxi/minibus back to the car. No ferry is required, which is why this is the gentler family gorge.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a Chania transfer tour if you do not want to manage the car-return logistics; the hike itself stays the same but the day becomes simpler.

  • Goody's Burger House — burgers, chicken burgers, fries, and junior menu fallback
  • Lithos Restaurant — beef burger with fries, grilled chicken, chicken/pork gyros, and skewers

days.heading: Samaria Gorge: full White Mountains descent

facts.label: Logistics
facts.valueHtml: Early KTEL from Chania; ANENDYK ferry out; return bus from Sougia/Sfakia

days.note: Samaria supplies a full mountain-to-sea day when the family wants the leg’s biggest hike. For the 8-year-old, the complete descent is conditional; the shorter route from Agia Roumeli toward the Iron Gates is the kid-friendlier substitute.

spots.name: Samaria Gorge — full Lefka Ori descent
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Samaria GorgeIG · Lefka OriFlickr

images.alt: The footbridge at the Iron Gates where Samaria Gorge pinches between towering walls
Tiny hikers dwarfed by the narrowest squeeze of the Samaria Gorge walls
The cypress-lined switchback descent into Samaria Gorge from Xyloskalo

spots.cost: Plan roughly EUR 65-EUR 100 family for park entry, KTEL buses, and ANENDYK ferry tickets if self-guided; guided transfers commonly price higher but simplify the bus/ferry chain. Bring cash for small add-ons in Agia Roumeli.
spots.climate: Mountain start, hot finish: Xyloskalo/Omalos starts around 1,200-1,250 m, but the lower gorge and Agia Roumeli can feel full-summer hot by afternoon. Start on the first practical Chania bus, carry 2L+ water per adult, hats, snacks, and real shoes.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use public logistics if everyone is comfortable with the sequence: early KTEL Chania -> Xyloskalo/Omalos, hike to Agia Roumeli, ANENDYK ferry to Sougia or Chora Sfakion, then the waiting KTEL bus back to Chania.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a guided transfer day if you want one throat to choke for ferry timing, bus seats, and pickup. It does not make the 16 km easier; it only removes logistics friction.
spots.restoHtml:
• Xyloskalo Restaurant — trailhead breakfast/coffee with the gorge view before the descent.
  • Faragi, Agia Roumeli — post-hike taverna; fries, grilled meat, simple pasta/rice-style kid orders.
  • Goody's Burger House Chania — late, plain burger/fries fallback after the long return.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lazy way from Agia Roumeli ↩ — ferry to Agia Roumeli, walk about an hour / ~2 km up to the Iron Gates, then return to the beach and ferry. This is the kid-friendly Samaria version if the full descent is too much.
  • Agia Roumeli beach ↗ — if you finish early, swim/eat before the 17:30 ferry window.
  • Limnoupolis Water Park ↗ — the no-guilt bailout if heat, legs, or ferry logistics are wrong.

spots.name: Funchal old town + Monte cable car + toboggans
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · FunchalIG · MonteFlickr

images.alt: Cable car gliding above Funchal's terracotta roofs

spots.cost: Cable car EUR 22 RT / EUR 16 one-way adult, ages 7-14 half price - one-way up for the family is ~EUR 48. Monte toboggan (2026 prices): EUR 40 per 2-person sled, cash only, closed Sundays - two sleds = EUR 80. Monte Palace garden EUR 18 adult, kids to 14 free.
spots.climate: June Funchal: 72-75 F days / 61-63 F nights, ~10 hours of sun and only ~5 rain days - one of the driest months on the island.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride the cable car one-way up (EUR 48, not EUR 76 RT), toboggan partway down, and finish by Bolt/taxi - the classic route that skips paying for the ride down twice.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The toboggan itself IS the splurge at EUR 80 for two wicker sleds - a 130-year-old tradition and the single most kid-memorable EUR 80 on the island.
