days.heading: Arieiro sunrise: Stairway to Heaven - weather shot 1 of 2
days.daycost: Est. $80-$220 - permits, fuel or transfer, lunch

facts.label: Permit
facts.valueHtml: PR1 EUR 10.50 pp, kids 12 and under free

days.note: The family version is the out-and-back from the Arieiro summit to Ninho da Manta and the staircase viewpoints (this first section is two-way; the full one-way traverse to Pico Ruivo is too strenuous for the 8-year-old). If the summit is in cloud, bail early and swap this with Saturday - that retry is exactly what the 4-night stay buys.

spots.name: Pico do Arieiro: Stairway to Heaven ridge (PR1)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Pico do ArieiroFlickr

images.alt: Pico do Arieiro ridge above a sea of clouds
Dramatic stairway ridge on Madeira's PR1 trail
Sunrise light across Pico Ruivo's jagged ridge

spots.cost: PR1 permit EUR 10.50 pp booked on SIMplifica (EUR 7 with a licensed operator); kids 12 and under free, so the family pays ~EUR 31.50. Summit parking free but full before sunrise on clear days. Shared sunrise transfer alternative: EUR 30-40 pp.
spots.climate: Pre-dawn summit (1,818 m): 41-50 F even in June - real jackets and hats. The sea-of-clouds inversion is a morning phenomenon; clouds typically swallow the peaks by afternoon. June is one of Madeira's driest months.
spots.saveHtml: Save Self-drive at 5:15 am instead of booking transfer seats: the family saves roughly $120-$160 and keeps the schedule flexible for the cloud lottery.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book the guided sunrise transfer (EUR 30-40 pp) if nobody wants to drive mountain hairpins in the dark - pickup ~5:00-5:30 am for a ~6:50 sunrise.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzaria Xaramba — old-town pizzeria by the fort; plain margherita is the safe order
  • Hamburgueria do Mercado — burgers and fries by the market; a plain burger runs about EUR 10
  • Il Basilico — Lido promenade Italian; pizza, plain pasta, and highchairs
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pico Ruivo from Achada do Teixeira (PR1.2) ↩ — the gentler back route to Madeira's highest summit - a real substitute if the PR1 first section is closed or the exposure feels like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Risco waterfall only ↗ — flatter Rabacal branch with a tall waterfall when 25 Fontes feels like too much walking.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.
spots.bloglinksHtml: PR1 reopening status (Apr 2026)SIMplifica trail permit rules

days.heading: 25 Fontes levada, then Camara de Lobos golden hour

facts.label: Late day
facts.valueHtml: Camara de Lobos + Cabo Girao skywalk

days.note: Levada walking is the flat, kid-friendly lower-exposure counterpoint to the alpine ridge day: water channels, tunnels of green, and a waterfall pool payoff. Bail to the short Risco branch if the 8-year-old is done. End with fishing boats and the 580 m skywalk on the way home.

spots.name: 25 Fontes + Risco levada (PR6, Rabacal)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · 25 FontesIG · RiscoFlickr

images.alt: Lush Laurissilva forest along Madeira's levada country
Viewpoint over the Ribeiro Frio green valleys
Shaded levada tunnel in Ribeiro Frio forest

spots.cost: Permit EUR 4.50 pp (kids 12 and under free) = ~EUR 13.50 family, booked on SIMplifica. Rabacal parking free; the access-road shuttle is EUR 5 one-way / EUR 8 return, cash only.
spots.climate: June: the Rabacal plateau sits in the cloud belt - expect cooler, mistier air than Funchal and pack a layer. Trails are mostly flat levada walking with ~300 m of stairs near the falls.
spots.saveHtml: Save Start before the ~10-11 am shuttle and walk the 2 km access road down (~40 min) - saves EUR 32 family and beats the crowds to the falls.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge None needed - this day is nearly free. If energy is high, add the 30-minute Risco waterfall branch (PR6.1) at no extra cost.
spots.restoHtml:
• Anonimo — some of the island's best Neapolitan pizza; margherita for the kids
  • Pizza Cafe (Camara de Lobos) — generous pizza and pasta portions steps from the harbor
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada house since 1966; grilled beef/chicken skewers, fries, and bolo do caco bread
spots.altboxHtml:
• Risco waterfall only (PR6.1) ↩ — the built-in bail-out: the Risco branch is a short, flat walk to a 100 m waterfall if the full 9-11 km round trip looks like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.
  • Ribeiro Frio and Balcoes ↗ — short, family-friendly forest walk with a big-view payoff if clouds cooperate.
spots.bloglinksHtml: PR6 trail guide and statusOfficial IFCN trail-fee FAQ

spots.name: Camara de Lobos + Cabo Girao Skywalk
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Camara de LobosIG · Cabo GiraoFlickr

images.alt: Atlantic view from Cabo Girao's glass skywalk
Layered Madeiran mountains and ravines
Colorful fishing boats in Camara de Lobos

spots.cost: Camara de Lobos harbor is free. Cabo Girao skywalk is EUR 5 pp since Jan 2026, kids 12 and under free - plan EUR 15 worst case (whether the 13-year-old is exempt is ambiguous in current sources).
spots.climate: June: the sunny south coast - 72-75 F afternoons. Golden hour is the move: fishing boats glow and the 580 m cliff view softens after the tour buses leave.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do this as the late-afternoon tail of the 25 Fontes day rather than a separate outing - it is 15 minutes from Funchal and needs no tickets beyond the skywalk.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge An espetada dinner at Santo Antonio in Estreito - the skewers-and-fries house the locals drive to, and a legitimately picky-kid-safe splurge.
spots.restoHtml:
• Anonimo — some of the island's best Neapolitan pizza; margherita for the kids
  • Pizza Cafe (Camara de Lobos) — generous pizza and pasta portions steps from the harbor
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada house since 1966; grilled beef/chicken skewers, fries, and bolo do caco bread
spots.altboxHtml:
• Ponta do Sol sunset ↩ — the island's sunniest village, 15 minutes further west - a good swap if the family wants a slower waterfront evening instead of the skywalk.

days.heading: Fanal fog forest + Porto Moniz lava pools

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Fanal - go only if there IS fog

days.note: This day has a double job: it is the ancient-forest-and-lava-pools loop, and it is the Arieiro backup slot. If Thursday's summit was clouded out, do the sunrise retry first and compress this loop into the afternoon. Fanal without fog is skippable; Porto Moniz is not.

spots.name: Fanal fog forest (Paul da Serra)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · FanalFlickr

images.alt: Wind-shaped ancient trees in Fanal's mist
Madeira waterfall framed by lush subtropical growth
Green Madeiran valley and cascading water

spots.cost: Currently free, with a large free lot at the Fanal forestry post. Since Jan 2026 access is designated-paths-only with a daily visitor cap; a paid-entry model is under study - verify closer to travel.
spots.climate: June: Fanal sits at ~1,150 m in the cloud belt - fog is most likely in the morning and on humid days, and June afternoons often burn clear. The fog IS the show; a clear Fanal is just a pasture with old trees.
spots.saveHtml: Save Fanal costs nothing - the save is sequencing. Check the webcams/weather that morning and only commit when fog is actually sitting on the plateau.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Nothing to buy here. Spend the saved money on lunch at the Porto Moniz pools 25 minutes downhill.
spots.restoHtml:

spots.altboxHtml:

days.heading: Imbros Gorge and south-coast swim
days.daycost: Est. $170-$330 - entrance, return ride/taxi, meals, fuel

facts.label: Hike
facts.valueHtml: 8km Imbros village -> Komitades; easier than Samaria

days.note: Imbros stays the family-accessible gorge: shorter, shadier, no ferry, and a good gut-check before deciding whether Samaria is a full descent or lazy-way outing on a later hiking day.

spots.name: Imbros Gorge + south-coast swim

spots.cost: Entrance is typically EUR 3-EUR 5 pp cash. If self-driving, start at Imbros village and arrange a Komitades-to-Imbros return taxi/minibus before you begin; shared rides are commonly about EUR 8 pp, or roughly EUR 25-35 for a small private taxi.

spots.saveHtml: Save Use the self-drive pattern: park at Imbros, walk down to Komitades, then take the pre-arranged local taxi/minibus back to the car. No ferry is required, which is why this is the gentler family gorge.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a Chania transfer tour if you do not want to manage the car-return logistics; the hike itself stays the same but the day becomes simpler.

days.heading: Samaria Gorge: full White Mountains descent

facts.label: Logistics
facts.valueHtml: Early KTEL from Chania; ANENDYK ferry out; return bus from Sougia/Sfakia

days.note: Samaria supplies a full mountain-to-sea day when the family wants the leg’s biggest hike. For the 8-year-old, the complete descent is conditional; the shorter route from Agia Roumeli toward the Iron Gates is the kid-friendlier substitute.

spots.name: Samaria Gorge — full Lefka Ori descent
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Samaria GorgeIG · Lefka OriFlickr

images.alt: The footbridge at the Iron Gates where Samaria Gorge pinches between towering walls
Tiny hikers dwarfed by the narrowest squeeze of the Samaria Gorge walls
The cypress-lined switchback descent into Samaria Gorge from Xyloskalo

spots.cost: Plan roughly EUR 65-EUR 100 family for park entry, KTEL buses, and ANENDYK ferry tickets if self-guided; guided transfers commonly price higher but simplify the bus/ferry chain. Bring cash for small add-ons in Agia Roumeli.
spots.climate: Mountain start, hot finish: Xyloskalo/Omalos starts around 1,200-1,250 m, but the lower gorge and Agia Roumeli can feel full-summer hot by afternoon. Start on the first practical Chania bus, carry 2L+ water per adult, hats, snacks, and real shoes.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use public logistics if everyone is comfortable with the sequence: early KTEL Chania -> Xyloskalo/Omalos, hike to Agia Roumeli, ANENDYK ferry to Sougia or Chora Sfakion, then the waiting KTEL bus back to Chania.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a guided transfer day if you want one throat to choke for ferry timing, bus seats, and pickup. It does not make the 16 km easier; it only removes logistics friction.
spots.restoHtml:
• Xyloskalo Restaurant — trailhead breakfast/coffee with the gorge view before the descent.
  • Faragi, Agia Roumeli — post-hike taverna; fries, grilled meat, simple pasta/rice-style kid orders.
  • Goody's Burger House Chania — late, plain burger/fries fallback after the long return.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lazy way from Agia Roumeli ↩ — ferry to Agia Roumeli, walk about an hour / ~2 km up to the Iron Gates, then return to the beach and ferry. This is the kid-friendly Samaria version if the full descent is too much.
  • Agia Roumeli beach ↗ — if you finish early, swim/eat before the 17:30 ferry window.
  • Limnoupolis Water Park ↗ — the no-guilt bailout if heat, legs, or ferry logistics are wrong.

days.heading: Arieiro sunrise: Stairway to Heaven - weather shot 1 of 2
days.daycost: Est. $80-$220 - permits, fuel or transfer, lunch

facts.label: Permit
facts.valueHtml: PR1 EUR 10.50 pp, kids 12 and under free

days.note: The family version is the out-and-back from the Arieiro summit to Ninho da Manta and the staircase viewpoints (this first section is two-way; the full one-way traverse to Pico Ruivo is too strenuous for the 8-year-old). spots.name: Pico do Arieiro: Stairway to Heaven ridge (PR1)

spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book the guided sunrise transfer (EUR 30-40 pp) if nobody wants to drive mountain hairpins in the dark - pickup ~5:00-5:30 am for a ~6:50 sunrise.

days.heading: Arieiro sunrise: Stairway to Heaven - weather shot 1 of 2
days.daycost: Est. $80-$220 - permits, fuel or transfer, lunch

facts.label: Permit
facts.valueHtml: PR1 EUR 10.50 pp, kids 12 and under free

days.note: The family version is the out-and-back from the Arieiro summit to Ninho da Manta and the staircase viewpoints (this first section is two-way; the full one-way traverse to Pico Ruivo is too strenuous for the 8-year-old). If the summit is in cloud, bail early and swap this with Saturday - that retry is exactly what the 4-night stay buys.

spots.name: Pico do Arieiro: Stairway to Heaven ridge (PR1)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Pico do ArieiroFlickr

images.alt: Pico do Arieiro ridge above a sea of clouds
Dramatic stairway ridge on Madeira's PR1 trail
Sunrise light across Pico Ruivo's jagged ridge

spots.cost: PR1 permit EUR 10.50 pp booked on SIMplifica (EUR 7 with a licensed operator); kids 12 and under free, so the family pays ~EUR 31.50. Summit parking free but full before sunrise on clear days. Shared sunrise transfer alternative: EUR 30-40 pp.
spots.climate: Pre-dawn summit (1,818 m): 41-50 F even in June - real jackets and hats. The sea-of-clouds inversion is a morning phenomenon; clouds typically swallow the peaks by afternoon. June is one of Madeira's driest months.
spots.saveHtml: Save Self-drive at 5:15 am instead of booking transfer seats: the family saves roughly $120-$160 and keeps the schedule flexible for the cloud lottery.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book the guided sunrise transfer (EUR 30-40 pp) if nobody wants to drive mountain hairpins in the dark - pickup ~5:00-5:30 am for a ~6:50 sunrise.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzaria Xaramba — old-town pizzeria by the fort; plain margherita is the safe order
  • Hamburgueria do Mercado — burgers and fries by the market; a plain burger runs about EUR 10
  • Il Basilico — Lido promenade Italian; pizza, plain pasta, and highchairs
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pico Ruivo from Achada do Teixeira (PR1.2) ↩ — the gentler back route to Madeira's highest summit - a real substitute if the PR1 first section is closed or the exposure feels like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Risco waterfall only ↗ — flatter Rabacal branch with a tall waterfall when 25 Fontes feels like too much walking.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.

days.note: Levada walking is the flat, kid-friendly lower-exposure counterpoint to the alpine ridge day: water channels, tunnels of green, and a waterfall pool payoff. Bail to the short Risco branch if the 8-year-old is done. End with fishing boats and the 580 m skywalk on the way home.

spots.climate: June: the Rabacal plateau sits in the cloud belt - expect cooler, mistier air than Funchal and pack a layer. Trails are mostly flat levada walking with ~300 m of stairs near the falls.
spots.saveHtml: Save Start before the ~10-11 am shuttle and walk the 2 km access road down (~40 min) - saves EUR 32 family and beats the crowds to the falls.

spots.altboxHtml:
• Risco waterfall only (PR6.1) ↩ — the built-in bail-out: the Risco branch is a short, flat walk to a 100 m waterfall if the full 9-11 km round trip looks like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.
  • Ribeiro Frio and Balcoes ↗ — short, family-friendly forest walk with a big-view payoff if clouds cooperate.

spots.saveHtml: Save Use a grocery breakfast, beach picnic, and apartment laundry. Four low-drama beach nights are cheaper than a full resort if you keep the lodging gate.

spots.climate: June Funchal: 72-75 F days / 61-63 F nights, ~10 hours of sun and only ~5 rain days - one of the driest months on the island.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride the cable car one-way up (EUR 48, not EUR 76 RT), toboggan partway down, and finish by Bolt/taxi - the classic route that skips paying for the ride down twice.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The toboggan itself IS the splurge at EUR 80 for two wicker sleds - a 130-year-old tradition and the single most kid-memorable EUR 80 on the island.
spots.restoHtml:

spots.altboxHtml:
• Mercado dos Lavradores + old-town painted doors ↩ — the free version of a Funchal afternoon: market fruit tasting upstairs, painted-door street art in the Zona Velha, gelato by the fort.
  • Jardim Botanico da Madeira ↗ — terraced gardens and city views; a good fog or heat substitute for higher viewpoints.

days.heading: Arieiro sunrise: Stairway to Heaven - weather shot 1 of 2
days.daycost: Est. $80-$220 - permits, fuel or transfer, lunch

facts.label: Permit
facts.valueHtml: PR1 EUR 10.50 pp, kids 12 and under free

days.note: The family version is the out-and-back from the Arieiro summit to Ninho da Manta and the staircase viewpoints (this first section is two-way; the full one-way traverse to Pico Ruivo is too strenuous for the 8-year-old). If the summit is in cloud, bail early and swap this with Saturday - that retry is exactly what the 4-night stay buys.

spots.name: Pico do Arieiro: Stairway to Heaven ridge (PR1)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Pico do ArieiroFlickr

images.alt: Pico do Arieiro ridge above a sea of clouds
Dramatic stairway ridge on Madeira's PR1 trail
Sunrise light across Pico Ruivo's jagged ridge

spots.cost: PR1 permit EUR 10.50 pp booked on SIMplifica (EUR 7 with a licensed operator); kids 12 and under free, so the family pays ~EUR 31.50. Summit parking free but full before sunrise on clear days. Shared sunrise transfer alternative: EUR 30-40 pp.
spots.climate: Pre-dawn summit (1,818 m): 41-50 F even in June - real jackets and hats. The sea-of-clouds inversion is a morning phenomenon; clouds typically swallow the peaks by afternoon. June is one of Madeira's driest months.
spots.saveHtml: Save Self-drive at 5:15 am instead of booking transfer seats: the family saves roughly $120-$160 and keeps the schedule flexible for the cloud lottery.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book the guided sunrise transfer (EUR 30-40 pp) if nobody wants to drive mountain hairpins in the dark - pickup ~5:00-5:30 am for a ~6:50 sunrise.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzaria Xaramba — old-town pizzeria by the fort; plain margherita is the safe order
  • Hamburgueria do Mercado — burgers and fries by the market; a plain burger runs about EUR 10
  • Il Basilico — Lido promenade Italian; pizza, plain pasta, and highchairs
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pico Ruivo from Achada do Teixeira (PR1.2) ↩ — the gentler back route to Madeira's highest summit - a real substitute if the PR1 first section is closed or the exposure feels like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Risco waterfall only ↗ — flatter Rabacal branch with a tall waterfall when 25 Fontes feels like too much walking.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.
spots.bloglinksHtml: PR1 reopening status (Apr 2026)SIMplifica trail permit rules

days.heading: 25 Fontes levada, then Camara de Lobos golden hour

facts.label: Late day
facts.valueHtml: Camara de Lobos + Cabo Girao skywalk

days.note: Levada walking is the flat, kid-friendly lower-exposure counterpoint to the alpine ridge day: water channels, tunnels of green, and a waterfall pool payoff. Bail to the short Risco branch if the 8-year-old is done. End with fishing boats and the 580 m skywalk on the way home.

spots.name: 25 Fontes + Risco levada (PR6, Rabacal)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · 25 FontesIG · RiscoFlickr

images.alt: Lush Laurissilva forest along Madeira's levada country
Viewpoint over the Ribeiro Frio green valleys
Shaded levada tunnel in Ribeiro Frio forest

spots.cost: Permit EUR 4.50 pp (kids 12 and under free) = ~EUR 13.50 family, booked on SIMplifica. Rabacal parking free; the access-road shuttle is EUR 5 one-way / EUR 8 return, cash only.
spots.climate: June: the Rabacal plateau sits in the cloud belt - expect cooler, mistier air than Funchal and pack a layer. Trails are mostly flat levada walking with ~300 m of stairs near the falls.
spots.saveHtml: Save Start before the ~10-11 am shuttle and walk the 2 km access road down (~40 min) - saves EUR 32 family and beats the crowds to the falls.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge None needed - this day is nearly free. If energy is high, add the 30-minute Risco waterfall branch (PR6.1) at no extra cost.
spots.restoHtml:
• Anonimo — some of the island's best Neapolitan pizza; margherita for the kids
  • Pizza Cafe (Camara de Lobos) — generous pizza and pasta portions steps from the harbor
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada house since 1966; grilled beef/chicken skewers, fries, and bolo do caco bread
spots.altboxHtml:
• Risco waterfall only (PR6.1) ↩ — the built-in bail-out: the Risco branch is a short, flat walk to a 100 m waterfall if the full 9-11 km round trip looks like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.
  • Ribeiro Frio and Balcoes ↗ — short, family-friendly forest walk with a big-view payoff if clouds cooperate.
spots.bloglinksHtml: PR6 trail guide and statusOfficial IFCN trail-fee FAQ

spots.name: Camara de Lobos + Cabo Girao Skywalk
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Camara de LobosIG · Cabo GiraoFlickr

images.alt: Atlantic view from Cabo Girao's glass skywalk
Layered Madeiran mountains and ravines
Colorful fishing boats in Camara de Lobos

spots.cost: Camara de Lobos harbor is free. Cabo Girao skywalk is EUR 5 pp since Jan 2026, kids 12 and under free - plan EUR 15 worst case (whether the 13-year-old is exempt is ambiguous in current sources).
spots.climate: June: the sunny south coast - 72-75 F afternoons. Golden hour is the move: fishing boats glow and the 580 m cliff view softens after the tour buses leave.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do this as the late-afternoon tail of the 25 Fontes day rather than a separate outing - it is 15 minutes from Funchal and needs no tickets beyond the skywalk.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge An espetada dinner at Santo Antonio in Estreito - the skewers-and-fries house the locals drive to, and a legitimately picky-kid-safe splurge.
spots.restoHtml:
• Anonimo — some of the island's best Neapolitan pizza; margherita for the kids
  • Pizza Cafe (Camara de Lobos) — generous pizza and pasta portions steps from the harbor
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada house since 1966; grilled beef/chicken skewers, fries, and bolo do caco bread
spots.altboxHtml:
• Ponta do Sol sunset ↩ — the island's sunniest village, 15 minutes further west - a good swap if the family wants a slower waterfront evening instead of the skywalk.
  • Santa Catarina Park ↗ — low-effort green space above the harbor for a quick kid reset before dinner.
  • Mercado dos Lavradores ↗ — colorful market + fruit stop in the old town when you want a lighter Funchal hour.

days.heading: Fanal fog forest + Porto Moniz lava pools

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Fanal - go only if there IS fog

days.note: This day has a double job: it is the ancient-forest-and-lava-pools loop, and it is the Arieiro backup slot. If Thursday's summit was clouded out, do the sunrise retry first and compress this loop into the afternoon. Fanal without fog is skippable; Porto Moniz is not.

spots.name: Fanal fog forest (Paul da Serra)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · FanalFlickr

images.alt: Wind-shaped ancient trees in Fanal's mist
Madeira waterfall framed by lush subtropical growth
Green Madeiran valley and cascading water

spots.cost: Currently free, with a large free lot at the Fanal forestry post. Since Jan 2026 access is designated-paths-only with a daily visitor cap; a paid-entry model is under study - verify closer to travel.
spots.climate: June: Fanal sits at ~1,150 m in the cloud belt - fog is most likely in the morning and on humid days, and June afternoons often burn clear. The fog IS the show; a clear Fanal is just a pasture with old trees.
spots.saveHtml: Save Fanal costs nothing - the save is sequencing. Check the webcams/weather that morning and only commit when fog is actually sitting on the plateau.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Nothing to buy here. Spend the saved money on lunch at the Porto Moniz pools 25 minutes downhill.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurante Cachalote — built on the lava rocks beside the pools; burgers and simple grills, the location does the work
  • Restaurante Orca — pool-view terrace; burgers and simple mains
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada-and-fries dinner stop on the drive back south via Encumeada
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sao Vicente valley drive ↩ — if the plateau is stubbornly clear, drop through the dramatic north-coast valley road instead and get to the pools early.
  • Pico Ruivo from Achada do Teixeira ↗ — shorter back-door summit route if the Arieiro ridge is closed, foggy, or too exposed.
  • Risco waterfall only ↗ — flatter Rabacal branch with a tall waterfall when 25 Fontes feels like too much walking.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Fanal 2026 access rulesFanal visitor guide

spots.name: Porto Moniz natural lava pools
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Porto MonizFlickr

images.alt: Atlantic waves beside Porto Moniz lava pools
Black volcanic lava along Madeira's north coast
Natural lava pools seen from above

spots.cost: EUR 3 pp for everyone age 3+ = EUR 12 family, open 9 am-7 pm in summer, with changing rooms, lockers, showers, lifeguards, and a snack bar. The rougher Cachalote pools on the west side are free.
spots.climate: June sea: ~70 F - brisk but swimmable, and the lava pools are calm even when the open Atlantic is rough. This is Madeira's one real swim stop.
spots.saveHtml: Save The paid pools are already the cheap option at EUR 12 for the family - bring towels and swim shoes and skip renting anything.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch on the rocks at Cachalote or Orca with the surf exploding behind the glass - pay for the view once.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurante Cachalote — built on the lava rocks beside the pools; burgers and simple grills, the location does the work
  • Restaurante Orca — pool-view terrace; burgers and simple mains
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada-and-fries dinner stop on the drive back south via Encumeada
spots.altboxHtml:
• Seixal natural pools + black-sand beach ↩ — smaller, wilder pools and a black-sand beach 15 minutes east - a quieter swap if Porto Moniz is packed.
  • Praia da Calheta ↗ — sheltered golden-sand beach; the easiest true sand-and-swim fallback on Madeira.
  • Faja dos Padres ↗ — cable-car descent to a quiet beach/vineyard terrace when the family wants a half-day adventure.

spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge None needed - this day is nearly free. If energy is high, add the 30-minute Risco waterfall branch (PR6.1) at no extra cost.
spots.restoHtml:
• Anonimo — some of the island's best Neapolitan pizza; margherita for the kids
  • Pizza Cafe (Camara de Lobos) — generous pizza and pasta portions steps from the harbor
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada house since 1966; grilled beef/chicken skewers, fries, and bolo do caco bread
spots.altboxHtml:
• Risco waterfall only (PR6.1) ↩ — the built-in bail-out: the Risco branch is a short, flat walk to a 100 m waterfall if the full 9-11 km round trip looks like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.
  • Ribeiro Frio and Balcoes ↗ — short, family-friendly forest walk with a big-view payoff if clouds cooperate.

spots.saveHtml: Save Do this as the late-afternoon tail of the 25 Fontes day rather than a separate outing - it is 15 minutes from Funchal and needs no tickets beyond the skywalk.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge An espetada dinner at Santo Antonio in Estreito - the skewers-and-fries house the locals drive to, and a legitimately picky-kid-safe splurge.
spots.restoHtml:

days.heading: Fanal fog forest + Porto Moniz lava pools

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Fanal - go only if there IS fog

days.note: This day has a double job: it is the ancient-forest-and-lava-pools loop, and it is the Arieiro backup slot. If Thursday's summit was clouded out, do the sunrise retry first and compress this loop into the afternoon. Fanal without fog is skippable; Porto Moniz is not.

spots.name: Fanal fog forest (Paul da Serra)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · FanalFlickr

images.alt: Wind-shaped ancient trees in Fanal's mist
Madeira waterfall framed by lush subtropical growth
Green Madeiran valley and cascading water

spots.cost: Currently free, with a large free lot at the Fanal forestry post. Since Jan 2026 access is designated-paths-only with a daily visitor cap; a paid-entry model is under study - verify closer to travel.
spots.climate: June: Fanal sits at ~1,150 m in the cloud belt - fog is most likely in the morning and on humid days, and June afternoons often burn clear. The fog IS the show; a clear Fanal is just a pasture with old trees.
spots.saveHtml: Save Fanal costs nothing - the save is sequencing. Check the webcams/weather that morning and only commit when fog is actually sitting on the plateau.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Nothing to buy here. Spend the saved money on lunch at the Porto Moniz pools 25 minutes downhill.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurante Cachalote — built on the lava rocks beside the pools; burgers and simple grills, the location does the work
  • Restaurante Orca — pool-view terrace; burgers and simple mains
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada-and-fries dinner stop on the drive back south via Encumeada
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sao Vicente valley drive ↩ — if the plateau is stubbornly clear, drop through the dramatic north-coast valley road instead and get to the pools early.
  • Pico Ruivo from Achada do Teixeira ↗ — shorter back-door summit route if the Arieiro ridge is closed, foggy, or too exposed.
  • Risco waterfall only ↗ — flatter Rabacal branch with a tall waterfall when 25 Fontes feels like too much walking.

spots.cost: EUR 3 pp for everyone age 3+ = EUR 12 family, open 9 am-7 pm in summer, with changing rooms, lockers, showers, lifeguards, and a snack bar. The rougher Cachalote pools on the west side are free.

spots.saveHtml: Save The paid pools are already the cheap option at EUR 12 for the family - bring towels and swim shoes and skip renting anything.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch on the rocks at Cachalote or Orca with the surf exploding behind the glass - pay for the view once.

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Pletna to Bled Island + Bled Castle

facts.label: Treat
facts.valueHtml: Bled cream cake (kremšnita) on a castle terrace

spots.name: Lake Bled: island church, pletna & clifftop castle
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lakebledIG · bledislandIG · sloveniaFlickr

images.alt: Bled island church silhouetted against a golden sunrise glow with a flawless symmetric reflection on the still lake, Julian Alps flanking the water.
Elevated panorama of the whole of Lake Bled at first light, the tiny island church mirrored in glowing water beneath the snow-dusted Julian Alps.
Bled Castle clinging to the top of a sheer vertical cliff above the lakeside town, autumn forest below and clear alpine sky beyond.

spots.cost: The pletna boat to the island is €20 adult / €10 child round trip (cash to the pletnar, ~20 min each way plus ~40 min on the island); the island church admission with the wishing bell is €12 adult / €5 child. Bled Castle is about €19 adult / €7 child. A family of four doing all three runs roughly €150 (~$165). Walking the lake shore, ringing nothing, and photographing the island is free.
spots.climate: ~1,500 ft, Julian Alps foothills. June highs are a pleasant ~24°C / mid-70s°F with frequent afternoon showers. The lake itself is a swimmable-but-cool ~18–19°C in June — fine for a quick dip off the grassy lidos, not a warm-water day (that waits for Piran).
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip the pletna and walk the 6 km lakeshore path for the classic island view for free; ring the wishing bell only if the kids insist. The castle courtyard view is the same whether or not you buy the museum ticket.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Do the full ritual: pletna across, 99 steps up, ring the bell, then a slice of Bled cream cake (kremšnita) on a castle terrace over the lake.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Rustika — wood-fired pizza with a kids’ pizza noted and simple pasta, a reliable picky-eater anchor
  • Pizzeria Gallus — big straightforward pizzas near the lake
  • Slaščičarna Šmon — the original Bled cream cake plus ice cream for a low-drama treat stop
spots.altboxHtml:
• Bled Castle first, island after if morning light is better on the water later.
  • Straž hill or Ojstrica viewpoint for the postcard aerial of the island without a drone.
  • Rent a rowboat instead of the pletna for a cheaper, more active crossing.

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Vintgar Gorge (book the online timed slot)

facts.label: Weather rule
facts.valueHtml: Shaded and cool - a good warm-or-showery-morning pick

days.note: The 1.6 km wooden boardwalk clings to the emerald Radovna over rapids to the Šum waterfall. Buy the timed online pass in advance — there are no tickets at the gate anymore — and go early to beat the buses.

spots.name: Vintgar Gorge: emerald boardwalk through the Radovna canyon
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · vintgargorgeIG · blejskivintgarIG · sloveniaFlickr

images.alt: The wooden boardwalk clings to the sheer cliff of Vintgar Gorge above a vivid emerald pool of the Radovna River in warm backlight.
Two hikers walk the cliffside walkway as the brilliant blue-emerald Radovna River rushes over rapids through the lush Vintgar Gorge.
Whitewater rapids of the Radovna River surge between towering moss-covered limestone canyon walls deep in Vintgar Gorge.

spots.cost: Entry is €15 adult / €5 child (up to 15) — about €40 (~$44) for the family. Since 2025 there are NO tickets at the gorge entrance: you must buy an online timed-slot pass in advance (or on-site only at the P1 Vintgar central parking before the shuttle). Miss your slot and you wait. Open April–October only; helmets are provided and mandatory.
spots.climate: Shaded river canyon. The 1.6 km wooden boardwalk hugs the emerald Radovna over rapids and pools, ending at the Šum waterfall. Cool and often damp underfoot — a smart pick on a warm or showery morning. About 45 minutes one way; fine for both kids, not for strollers.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the earliest online slot to beat the tour buses and the midday crush, and walk back the upper forest loop rather than paying for the shuttle.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pair it with the nearby St Catherine’s church hilltop or the Pokljuka plateau for a bigger half-day in the Bled backcountry.
spots.restoHtml:
• Gostilna Vintgar (at the entrance) — simple grilled plates, fries, and pizza right by the exit
  • Pizzeria Rustika (Bled, ~10 min) — the dependable kids’-pizza fallback back in town
  • Bled lakeside kiosks — ice cream and quick bites after the walk
spots.altboxHtml:
• Come at opening or late afternoon — midday is the crowd peak on the narrow boardwalk.
  • Tolmin or Great Soča gorges later if you want a second, different canyon on the Soča leg.
  • Skip if heavy rain closes or slicks the boardwalk — it’s a fair-weather walk.

days.heading: Lake Bohinj + Vogel

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Vogel cable car over Triglav National Park

days.note: Quieter and wilder than Bled, deep in Triglav National Park: the Vogel cable car for the big peak panorama, the Savica waterfall walk, and a glassy lake for a kayak. Pack a layer for the summit and repack tonight for the Vršič crossing.

spots.name: Lake Bohinj: Vogel cable car + Savica Waterfall
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lakebohinjIG · vogelIG · triglavnationalparkFlickr

images.alt: The Church of St John the Baptist and the stone arch bridge at Ribcev Laz mirrored in a glassy Lake Bohinj under a streaked sunset sky.
The A-shaped Savica waterfall splits over a grey limestone cliff and plunges into its emerald pool deep in the Triglav gorge.
The sweeping view from the Vogel cable car looking down over Lake Bohinj to the Bohinj basin and the Julian Alps beyond.

spots.cost: Quieter and wilder than Bled, inside Triglav National Park (no park entry fee). The Vogel cable car is about €33 adult / €16 child return for a huge balcony view over the lake to the Triglav massif. Savica Waterfall is a ~€4 walk-in on a stepped path. Kayak or SUP rental on the lake runs ~€15–20/hour. The lakeshore and the stone bridge at Ribčev Laz are free.
spots.climate: Glacial lake, deeper in the park. Bohinj is colder than Bled — high-teens °C water even in June — and can catch mountain cloud. The Vogel top station sits above 1,500 m, so pack a layer even on a warm valley day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free lakeshore walk and the Savica path, and skip the cable car if the summit is clouded — the view is the whole point of the ticket.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Ride Vogel on a clear morning for the Triglav panorama, then kayak the glassy east end of the lake in the afternoon.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzerija Ema — very family-friendly with a small playground and coloring for kids, wood-fired pizza
  • Pizzeria Ukanc — large simple pizzas at the quiet Ukanc (west) end of the lake
  • Slaščičarna at Ribčev Laz — ice cream and pancakes by the bridge
spots.altboxHtml:
• Savica + lakeshore only as a gentle half-day if the peaks are socked in.
  • Mostnica Gorge (Stara Fužina) for a shorter, cheaper canyon walk with a cow-shaped rock the kids hunt for.
  • Panoramic lake boat instead of the cable car for a low-effort option.

days.heading: Vršič Pass to the Soča Valley

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Vršič Pass (1611 m), Russian Chapel, Lake Jasna

facts.label: Risk check
facts.valueHtml: Confirm the pass is open on promet.si; Predel is the fallback

days.note: The scenic transfer that earns its own day: over the Vršič Pass’s 50 numbered hairpins, past the WWI Russian Chapel and turquoise Lake Jasna, down to the emerald Soča. Check the pass is clear before setting off; if late snow has it shut, loop via Predel/Tarvisio.

spots.name: Vršič Pass: 50 hairpins over the roof of Slovenia
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · vrsicpassIG · julianalpsIG · socavalleyFlickr

images.alt: The bronze Zlatorog ibex statue perches on rocks above the turquoise water of Lake Jasna as the jagged Julian Alps catch first light behind.
A cobblestoned hairpin of the historic Russian Road on the Vrsic Pass curves past a dressed-stone retaining wall through the alpine forest.
The twin onion-domed wooden Russian Chapel stands among green spring larches at the foot of the Vrsic Pass, reached by a stone stairway.

spots.cost: Free to drive — the pass is a regional mountain road, so no vignette or toll applies. The only costs are fuel and your nerves on 50 numbered hairpins (24 up from Kranjska Gora, 26 down to the Soča). Budget the whole day for it: the Russian Chapel, the summit, Lake Jasna, and a dozen pull-offs.
spots.climate: 1,611 m — Slovenia’s highest road pass. Normally fully open and clear by mid-June, but this is the one real timing risk of the trip: late-lying snow can delay the spring clearing and there is no guaranteed open-by date. Check promet.si and the Erjavčeva koča cameras before committing; the Predel/Tarvisio route is the fallback if it’s shut.
spots.saveHtml: Save It’s a free scenic drive — pack a picnic for the summit and let the road be the day’s main event rather than paying for anything up top.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Stop at Erjavčeva koča near the top for štruklji and a hot chocolate with the peaks overhead, and detour to turquoise Lake Jasna on the descent.
spots.restoHtml:
• Erjavčeva koča (near the summit) — mountain-hut plates, štruklji, soups, and simple kid food with a view
  • Okrepčevalnica Loka (Trenta) — casual grill and pizza on the Soča side of the pass
  • Pack a picnic — the smartest move for the summit and the pull-offs
spots.altboxHtml:
• Predel Pass via Tarvisio (Italy) as the ~2–2.5 hr fallback if Vršič is closed — still Schengen, no border stop.
  • Lake Jasna (Kranjska Gora side) for an easy turquoise-water photo stop with the ibex statue.
  • Soča Trail / river source (Trenta) for a short leg-stretch on the way down.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Vršič Pass road status (Erjavčeva koča)Live road conditions — promet.si

days.travelNote: Scenic transfer - Bled to Bovec over Vršič Pass (or Predel if closed).

days.heading: Soča Valley water day
days.feel: Emerald river, rafting, the Great Gorge

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Family rafting + Great Soča Gorge + Kozjak Waterfall

facts.label: Water truth
facts.valueHtml: Soča is a glacial 11-15°C - wetsuits, not casual swimming

days.note: The adventure heart of the trip: guided rafting on the impossibly green Soča (a gentle family stretch for the 8-year-old, the standard run for the 13-year-old), then the free Great Soča Gorge and the easy Kozjak Waterfall walk. Book the water for the morning ahead of afternoon storms.

spots.name: Soča Valley: emerald river, family rafting & the Great Gorge
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · socariverIG · bovecIG · raftingFlickr

images.alt: Aerial view of the emerald Soča river looping in giant turquoise bends around the red-roofed town of Most na Soči deep in its green valley.
Two paddlers in red and blue kayaks gliding over the impossibly clear turquoise water of the Soča river between pale boulders.
The Great Soča Gorge (Velika korita) narrow slot of vivid turquoise water winding between sunlit golden and white limestone cliffs.

spots.cost: The impossibly emerald Soča is the heart of the leg. Guided rafting runs roughly €45–80/person plus a ~€6 river permit; standard trips take ages 8+ (the 13-year-old is fine), while a dedicated family/panoramic float suits the 8-year-old. The Great Soča Gorge (Velika korita) has free parking and no entry fee; Kozjak Waterfall is €5 adult / €3 child on an easy 3.3 km forest walk.
spots.climate: Glacial river, cold year-round. The Soča is a stunning ~11–15°C even in summer — perfect for wetsuit rafting, too cold for casual kid swimming beyond a shriek-and-out dip. June valley air is warm; afternoon thunderstorms are common, so book water sports for the morning.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free Great Soča Gorge boardwalk and the cheap Kozjak Waterfall walk, and pick the shorter family rafting stretch rather than the full-day trip.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book the guided rafting for the whole family (wetsuits included) and add the Boka waterfall viewpoint or a via-ferrata taster for the 13-year-old.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Črna Ovca (“Black Sheep”), Bovec — widely praised oven-baked pizza, English-speaking staff
  • Ristorante Pizzeria Papillo, Bovec — family-friendly and fast, plain pizza/pasta guaranteed
  • Letni Vrt, Bovec — pizza-focused garden spot for an easy dinner
spots.altboxHtml:
• Family/panoramic raft (Čezsoča stretch) for the 8-year-old instead of the standard run.
  • Great Soča Gorge + Kozjak as a no-rafting, low-cost water day.
  • Kobarid WWI museum + Napoleon Bridge for a rainy-morning indoor pivot.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Bovec family rafting & agesSoča Valley tourism

days.heading: Tolmin Gorges
days.feel: Devil’s Bridge and the park’s lowest canyon

facts.label: Option
facts.valueHtml: Bovec zipline / Kobarid WWI museum add-ons

days.note: A cooler canyon walk to close the Soča leg: the Devil’s Bridge high over the river, the thermal spring at the confluence, and Dante’s Cave. Add the Bovec zipline for the 13-year-old (height/weight limits apply) or the Kobarid museum if it rains.

spots.name: Tolmin Gorges: Devil’s Bridge & the Triglav park’s lowest canyon
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · tolmingorgesIG · tolminskakoritaIG · socavalleyFlickr

images.alt: The vivid turquoise Tolminka river snaking through the deep, narrow Tolmin gorge between towering moss-draped limestone walls.
The Devil's Bridge (Hudičev most) spanning high across the top of the Tolmin gorge above the turquoise Tolminka, with the cliff-side boardwalk below.
Turquoise water of the Tolminka rushing over pale rocks at the confluence in Tolmin gorge, framed by moss-covered ledges and forest.

spots.cost: Entry is €12 adult / €6 child (6–15) in high season — about €36 (~$40) for the family — on a one-hour timed slot. The loop takes in the Devil’s Bridge (60 m above the river), the thermal spring at the Tolminka–Zadlaščica confluence, and Dante’s Cave. Open roughly April–October; it closes only in exceptional high water, and tickets are refundable if it does.
spots.climate: Lowest entry point into Triglav National Park. A cooler, shaded canyon walk — a good hot-afternoon pick. The narrow paths and stairs are fine for both kids but not for strollers. After heavy rain the Tolminka can rise and force a closure, so keep it weather-flexible.
spots.saveHtml: Save It’s already cheap — just go early for your slot and bring water; the thermal-spring pool is a free cool-off.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the nearby Javorca memorial church or a Tolmin town gelato, or combine with the Kozjak Waterfall for a two-canyon day.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Cinca Marinca, Tolmin — casual pizza and pasta in town
  • Gostilna Rajht (Kobarid, ~20 min) — hearty local plates with simpler kid options
  • Tolmin bakeries — burek and pastries for a cheap trail lunch
spots.altboxHtml:
• Great Soča Gorge instead if you’d rather a free, shorter canyon walk.
  • Tolmin thermal spring pool for a quick kid cool-off inside the gorge.
  • Skip in high water — check the gorge’s status line before driving over.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Tolmin Gorges — pricelist & hoursTolmin Gorges info

days.heading: Drive to the coast via Škocjan Caves

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Škocjan Caves (UNESCO) en route to Piran

days.note: The Alps-to-coast transition, broken by the UNESCO Škocjan Caves — a vast underground canyon crossed by a footbridge high over the Reka. It sits right on the route to Piran, so it’s a marquee stop, not a detour. Arrive on the coast for the first warm-water evening.

spots.name: Škocjan Caves: an underground canyon bridged high over the Reka
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · skocjancavesIG · skocjanskejameIG · unescoFlickr

images.alt: The Škocjan collapse doline, a huge cliff-walled green sinkhole plunging to the cave mouth with a hilltop church on the forested rim.
The Cerkvenik footbridge spanning the vast illuminated underground canyon of the Škocjan Caves, high above the Reka river gorge.
An illuminated chamber of Postojna Cave (the easier alternative near Škocjan), a towering stalagmite column and stalactite-draped walls glowing amber above a lone visitor for scale.

spots.cost: The UNESCO show-stopper on the drive to the coast. The Underground Canyon tour is about €22–24 adult / €12.50 child in summer — roughly €70 (~$77) for the family — with departures around 10:00, 11:30, 13:00, 14:00, 15:00. It’s a 5 km, ~1,000-step, 2.5–3 hr walk crossing the famous Cerkvenik footbridge high above the Reka. Interior is ~12°C; no photography inside.
spots.climate: ~12°C underground, year-round. Bring a layer even on a hot coastal day. This is a genuinely strenuous walk, not a stroll, and not stroller-accessible — fine for a capable 8-year-old but a real hike. The early-exit option at the Big Collapse Doline shortens it to ~3 km.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take the standard Underground Canyon tour rather than any combo add-ons; the collapse-doline early exit trims the steps if legs are tired.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge If the 8-year-old would prefer easier magic, swap to Postojna Cave’s ride-in cave train — less dramatic than Škocjan’s canyon, but stroller-adaptable and a kid hit.
spots.restoHtml:
• Gostilna near the park entrance — simple grilled plates and pizza before the drive on
  • Divača bakeries (~10 min) — burek and pastries for a car snack
  • Piran/Portorož dinner — save the real meal for arrival on the coast
spots.altboxHtml:
• Postojna Cave as the easier, train-served alternative for younger kids.
  • Predjama Castle combined with Postojna if you pivot inland.
  • Big Collapse Doline early exit to cut the tour short without missing the canyon.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Škocjan Caves — tours & ticketsŠkocjan vs Postojna for kids

days.heading: Piran old town
days.feel: Venetian lanes and the first Adriatic swim

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Tartini Square, town walls, St George’s bell tower

facts.label: Payoff
facts.valueHtml: Sea ~22°C / 72°F - the warm-water leg the trip builds to

days.note: The reward after the mountains: a Venetian peninsula of red roofs and narrow lanes, the town-wall panorama, and the first proper Adriatic swim off the Punta rocks. Warmer and calmer than the Atlantic plans, if honestly a refreshing 72°F rather than tropical.

spots.name: Piran: a Venetian peninsula and the first warm Adriatic swim
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · piranIG · slovenianistriaIG · adriaticFlickr

images.alt: Golden-hour aerial of Piran's red-roofed peninsula jutting into the Adriatic, St George's church and bell tower glowing above the harbor.
Elevated view over Piran's whole peninsula and bell tower from St George's hill, a seagull gliding above the calm blue Adriatic.
Aerial view of Piran's oval Tartini Square with the Tartini statue, ringed by terracotta roofs, the marina and the open Adriatic beyond.
images.credit: Pham Ngoc Anh · Google Images source

spots.cost: Wandering Tartini Square, the harbor, and the tangle of Venetian lanes is free. The town walls are €3 adult / €2 student (under-12 free) for the best red-roof panorama; St George’s bell tower is ~€3 to climb its 146 steps. Piran’s own shoreline is rocky bathing platforms with ladders into deep water — the warm-water payoff of the whole trip, if a cooler-than-tropical one.
spots.climate: Northern Adriatic. June air is a warm ~25–28°C / high-70s°F, and the sea is about ~22°C / 72°F — genuinely swimmable but refreshing, not bathwater, especially early June. This is warmer and calmer than the Atlantic beaches on the Portugal-style plans, and the honest ceiling on this trip’s swimming.
spots.saveHtml: Save Swim free off the Punta rocks or the concrete platforms along Prešernovo nabrežje, and climb the €3 walls at golden hour instead of a pricier boat trip.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A sunset seafood dinner on the Piran waterfront, then the bell-tower climb for the 360° over the peninsula as the lights come on.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Porto Konoba — among the best pizza on the Slovenian coast, plus simple seafood
  • Pizzeria Burin — straightforward pizza with a sea view and family-friendly staff
  • Fritolin pri Cantini — casual order-at-the-counter fried calamari and simple plates at fair prices
spots.altboxHtml:
• Fiesa beach (15-min walk) for easier pebble-beach family swimming.
  • Piran town walls at sunset for the red-roof panorama without midday heat.
  • Boat or kayak to the cliffs for a calm-water paddle off the peninsula.

days.heading: Lake Bled
days.feel: Island church, pletna, and the clifftop castle

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Pletna to Bled Island + Bled Castle

facts.label: Treat
facts.valueHtml: Bled cream cake (kremšnita) on a castle terrace

days.note: The postcard day: a pletna boat to the island church and wishing bell, then up to the clifftop castle for the view down the lake. The iconic Slovenia image, and an easy one for the kids.

spots.name: Lake Bled: island church, pletna & clifftop castle
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lakebledIG · bledislandIG · sloveniaFlickr

images.alt: Bled island church silhouetted against a golden sunrise glow with a flawless symmetric reflection on the still lake, Julian Alps flanking the water.
Elevated panorama of the whole of Lake Bled at first light, the tiny island church mirrored in glowing water beneath the snow-dusted Julian Alps.
Bled Castle clinging to the top of a sheer vertical cliff above the lakeside town, autumn forest below and clear alpine sky beyond.

spots.cost: The pletna boat to the island is €20 adult / €10 child round trip (cash to the pletnar, ~20 min each way plus ~40 min on the island); the island church admission with the wishing bell is €12 adult / €5 child. Bled Castle is about €19 adult / €7 child. A family of four doing all three runs roughly €150 (~$165). Walking the lake shore, ringing nothing, and photographing the island is free.
spots.climate: ~1,500 ft, Julian Alps foothills. June highs are a pleasant ~24°C / mid-70s°F with frequent afternoon showers. The lake itself is a swimmable-but-cool ~18–19°C in June — fine for a quick dip off the grassy lidos, not a warm-water day (that waits for Piran).
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip the pletna and walk the 6 km lakeshore path for the classic island view for free; ring the wishing bell only if the kids insist. The castle courtyard view is the same whether or not you buy the museum ticket.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Do the full ritual: pletna across, 99 steps up, ring the bell, then a slice of Bled cream cake (kremšnita) on a castle terrace over the lake.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Rustika — wood-fired pizza with a kids’ pizza noted and simple pasta, a reliable picky-eater anchor
  • Pizzeria Gallus — big straightforward pizzas near the lake
  • Slaščičarna Šmon — the original Bled cream cake plus ice cream for a low-drama treat stop
spots.altboxHtml:
• Bled Castle first, island after if morning light is better on the water later.
  • Straž hill or Ojstrica viewpoint for the postcard aerial of the island without a drone.
  • Rent a rowboat instead of the pletna for a cheaper, more active crossing.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Bled Island — official pricelistBled tourism

days.heading: Vintgar Gorge

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Vintgar Gorge (book the online timed slot)

facts.label: Weather rule
facts.valueHtml: Shaded and cool - a good warm-or-showery-morning pick

days.note: The 1.6 km wooden boardwalk clings to the emerald Radovna over rapids to the Šum waterfall. Buy the timed online pass in advance — there are no tickets at the gate anymore — and go early to beat the buses.

spots.name: Vintgar Gorge: emerald boardwalk through the Radovna canyon
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · vintgargorgeIG · blejskivintgarIG · sloveniaFlickr

images.alt: The wooden boardwalk clings to the sheer cliff of Vintgar Gorge above a vivid emerald pool of the Radovna River in warm backlight.
Two hikers walk the cliffside walkway as the brilliant blue-emerald Radovna River rushes over rapids through the lush Vintgar Gorge.
Whitewater rapids of the Radovna River surge between towering moss-covered limestone canyon walls deep in Vintgar Gorge.

spots.cost: Entry is €15 adult / €5 child (up to 15) — about €40 (~$44) for the family. Since 2025 there are NO tickets at the gorge entrance: you must buy an online timed-slot pass in advance (or on-site only at the P1 Vintgar central parking before the shuttle). Miss your slot and you wait. Open April–October only; helmets are provided and mandatory.
spots.climate: Shaded river canyon. The 1.6 km wooden boardwalk hugs the emerald Radovna over rapids and pools, ending at the Šum waterfall. Cool and often damp underfoot — a smart pick on a warm or showery morning. About 45 minutes one way; fine for both kids, not for strollers.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the earliest online slot to beat the tour buses and the midday crush, and walk back the upper forest loop rather than paying for the shuttle.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pair it with the nearby St Catherine’s church hilltop or the Pokljuka plateau for a bigger half-day in the Bled backcountry.
spots.restoHtml:
• Gostilna Vintgar (at the entrance) — simple grilled plates, fries, and pizza right by the exit
  • Pizzeria Rustika (Bled, ~10 min) — the dependable kids’-pizza fallback back in town
  • Bled lakeside kiosks — ice cream and quick bites after the walk
spots.altboxHtml:
• Come at opening or late afternoon — midday is the crowd peak on the narrow boardwalk.
  • Tolmin or Great Soča gorges later if you want a second, different canyon on the Soča leg.
  • Skip if heavy rain closes or slicks the boardwalk — it’s a fair-weather walk.

days.heading: Lake Bohinj + Vogel

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Vogel cable car over Triglav National Park

days.note: Quieter and wilder than Bled, deep in Triglav National Park: the Vogel cable car for the big peak panorama, the Savica waterfall walk, and a glassy lake for a kayak. Pack a layer for the summit and repack tonight for the Vršič crossing.

spots.name: Lake Bohinj: Vogel cable car + Savica Waterfall
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lakebohinjIG · vogelIG · triglavnationalparkFlickr

images.alt: The Church of St John the Baptist and the stone arch bridge at Ribcev Laz mirrored in a glassy Lake Bohinj under a streaked sunset sky.
The A-shaped Savica waterfall splits over a grey limestone cliff and plunges into its emerald pool deep in the Triglav gorge.
The sweeping view from the Vogel cable car looking down over Lake Bohinj to the Bohinj basin and the Julian Alps beyond.

spots.cost: Quieter and wilder than Bled, inside Triglav National Park (no park entry fee). The Vogel cable car is about €33 adult / €16 child return for a huge balcony view over the lake to the Triglav massif. Savica Waterfall is a ~€4 walk-in on a stepped path. Kayak or SUP rental on the lake runs ~€15–20/hour. The lakeshore and the stone bridge at Ribčev Laz are free.
spots.climate: Glacial lake, deeper in the park. Bohinj is colder than Bled — high-teens °C water even in June — and can catch mountain cloud. The Vogel top station sits above 1,500 m, so pack a layer even on a warm valley day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free lakeshore walk and the Savica path, and skip the cable car if the summit is clouded — the view is the whole point of the ticket.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Ride Vogel on a clear morning for the Triglav panorama, then kayak the glassy east end of the lake in the afternoon.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzerija Ema — very family-friendly with a small playground and coloring for kids, wood-fired pizza
  • Pizzeria Ukanc — large simple pizzas at the quiet Ukanc (west) end of the lake
  • Slaščičarna at Ribčev Laz — ice cream and pancakes by the bridge
spots.altboxHtml:
• Savica + lakeshore only as a gentle half-day if the peaks are socked in.
  • Mostnica Gorge (Stara Fužina) for a shorter, cheaper canyon walk with a cow-shaped rock the kids hunt for.
  • Panoramic lake boat instead of the cable car for a low-effort option.

days.heading: Vršič Pass to the Soča Valley

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Vršič Pass (1611 m), Russian Chapel, Lake Jasna

facts.label: Risk check
facts.valueHtml: Confirm the pass is open on promet.si; Predel is the fallback

days.note: The scenic transfer that earns its own day: over the Vršič Pass’s 50 numbered hairpins, past the WWI Russian Chapel and turquoise Lake Jasna, down to the emerald Soča. Check the pass is clear before setting off; if late snow has it shut, loop via Predel/Tarvisio.

spots.name: Vršič Pass: 50 hairpins over the roof of Slovenia
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · vrsicpassIG · julianalpsIG · socavalleyFlickr

images.alt: The bronze Zlatorog ibex statue perches on rocks above the turquoise water of Lake Jasna as the jagged Julian Alps catch first light behind.
A cobblestoned hairpin of the historic Russian Road on the Vrsic Pass curves past a dressed-stone retaining wall through the alpine forest.
The twin onion-domed wooden Russian Chapel stands among green spring larches at the foot of the Vrsic Pass, reached by a stone stairway.

spots.cost: Free to drive — the pass is a regional mountain road, so no vignette or toll applies. The only costs are fuel and your nerves on 50 numbered hairpins (24 up from Kranjska Gora, 26 down to the Soča). Budget the whole day for it: the Russian Chapel, the summit, Lake Jasna, and a dozen pull-offs.
spots.climate: 1,611 m — Slovenia’s highest road pass. Normally fully open and clear by mid-June, but this is the one real timing risk of the trip: late-lying snow can delay the spring clearing and there is no guaranteed open-by date. Check promet.si and the Erjavčeva koča cameras before committing; the Predel/Tarvisio route is the fallback if it’s shut.
spots.saveHtml: Save It’s a free scenic drive — pack a picnic for the summit and let the road be the day’s main event rather than paying for anything up top.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Stop at Erjavčeva koča near the top for štruklji and a hot chocolate with the peaks overhead, and detour to turquoise Lake Jasna on the descent.
spots.restoHtml:
• Erjavčeva koča (near the summit) — mountain-hut plates, štruklji, soups, and simple kid food with a view
  • Okrepčevalnica Loka (Trenta) — casual grill and pizza on the Soča side of the pass
  • Pack a picnic — the smartest move for the summit and the pull-offs
spots.altboxHtml:
• Predel Pass via Tarvisio (Italy) as the ~2–2.5 hr fallback if Vršič is closed — still Schengen, no border stop.
  • Lake Jasna (Kranjska Gora side) for an easy turquoise-water photo stop with the ibex statue.
  • Soča Trail / river source (Trenta) for a short leg-stretch on the way down.

days.heading: Soča Valley water day
days.feel: Emerald river, rafting, the Great Gorge

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: Family rafting + Great Soča Gorge + Kozjak Waterfall

facts.label: Water truth
facts.valueHtml: Soča is a glacial 11-15°C - wetsuits, not casual swimming

days.note: The adventure heart of the trip: guided rafting on the impossibly green Soča (a gentle family stretch for the 8-year-old, the standard run for the 13-year-old), then the free Great Soča Gorge and the easy Kozjak Waterfall walk. Book the water for the morning ahead of afternoon storms.

spots.name: Soča Valley: emerald river, family rafting & the Great Gorge
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · socariverIG · bovecIG · raftingFlickr

images.alt: Aerial view of the emerald Soča river looping in giant turquoise bends around the red-roofed town of Most na Soči deep in its green valley.
Two paddlers in red and blue kayaks gliding over the impossibly clear turquoise water of the Soča river between pale boulders.
The Great Soča Gorge (Velika korita) narrow slot of vivid turquoise water winding between sunlit golden and white limestone cliffs.

spots.cost: The impossibly emerald Soča is the heart of the leg. Guided rafting runs roughly €45–80/person plus a ~€6 river permit; standard trips take ages 8+ (the 13-year-old is fine), while a dedicated family/panoramic float suits the 8-year-old. The Great Soča Gorge (Velika korita) has free parking and no entry fee; Kozjak Waterfall is €5 adult / €3 child on an easy 3.3 km forest walk.
spots.climate: Glacial river, cold year-round. The Soča is a stunning ~11–15°C even in summer — perfect for wetsuit rafting, too cold for casual kid swimming beyond a shriek-and-out dip. June valley air is warm; afternoon thunderstorms are common, so book water sports for the morning.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free Great Soča Gorge boardwalk and the cheap Kozjak Waterfall walk, and pick the shorter family rafting stretch rather than the full-day trip.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book the guided rafting for the whole family (wetsuits included) and add the Boka waterfall viewpoint or a via-ferrata taster for the 13-year-old.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Črna Ovca (“Black Sheep”), Bovec — widely praised oven-baked pizza, English-speaking staff
  • Ristorante Pizzeria Papillo, Bovec — family-friendly and fast, plain pizza/pasta guaranteed
  • Letni Vrt, Bovec — pizza-focused garden spot for an easy dinner
spots.altboxHtml:
• Family/panoramic raft (Čezsoča stretch) for the 8-year-old instead of the standard run.
  • Great Soča Gorge + Kozjak as a no-rafting, low-cost water day.
  • Kobarid WWI museum + Napoleon Bridge for a rainy-morning indoor pivot.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Bovec family rafting & agesSoča Valley tourism

days.heading: Tolmin Gorges
days.feel: Devil’s Bridge and the park’s lowest canyon

facts.label: Option
facts.valueHtml: Bovec zipline / Kobarid WWI museum add-ons

days.note: A cooler canyon walk to close the Soča leg: the Devil’s Bridge high over the river, the thermal spring at the confluence, and Dante’s Cave. Add the Bovec zipline for the 13-year-old (height/weight limits apply) or the Kobarid museum if it rains.

spots.name: Tolmin Gorges: Devil’s Bridge & the Triglav park’s lowest canyon
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · tolmingorgesIG · tolminskakoritaIG · socavalleyFlickr

images.alt: The vivid turquoise Tolminka river snaking through the deep, narrow Tolmin gorge between towering moss-draped limestone walls.
The Devil's Bridge (Hudičev most) spanning high across the top of the Tolmin gorge above the turquoise Tolminka, with the cliff-side boardwalk below.
Turquoise water of the Tolminka rushing over pale rocks at the confluence in Tolmin gorge, framed by moss-covered ledges and forest.

spots.cost: Entry is €12 adult / €6 child (6–15) in high season — about €36 (~$40) for the family — on a one-hour timed slot. The loop takes in the Devil’s Bridge (60 m above the river), the thermal spring at the Tolminka–Zadlaščica confluence, and Dante’s Cave. Open roughly April–October; it closes only in exceptional high water, and tickets are refundable if it does.
spots.climate: Lowest entry point into Triglav National Park. A cooler, shaded canyon walk — a good hot-afternoon pick. The narrow paths and stairs are fine for both kids but not for strollers. After heavy rain the Tolminka can rise and force a closure, so keep it weather-flexible.
spots.saveHtml: Save It’s already cheap — just go early for your slot and bring water; the thermal-spring pool is a free cool-off.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the nearby Javorca memorial church or a Tolmin town gelato, or combine with the Kozjak Waterfall for a two-canyon day.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Cinca Marinca, Tolmin — casual pizza and pasta in town
  • Gostilna Rajht (Kobarid, ~20 min) — hearty local plates with simpler kid options
  • Tolmin bakeries — burek and pastries for a cheap trail lunch
spots.altboxHtml:
• Great Soča Gorge instead if you’d rather a free, shorter canyon walk.
  • Tolmin thermal spring pool for a quick kid cool-off inside the gorge.
  • Skip in high water — check the gorge’s status line before driving over.

facts.valueHtml: Trümmelbach is inside the rock — the smart rainy-morning pick

spots.name: Lauterbrunnen valley: 72 waterfalls + Trümmelbach
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lauterbrunnenIG · staubbachIG · trummelbachFlickr

images.alt: Lauterbrunnen valley at dusk with a silky river and snow peaks between the cliffs

spots.cost: Staubbach Falls is free from the village. Trümmelbach Falls (the glacier torrents inside the mountain) charges about CHF 18 adult / CHF 8 child 6–15 — roughly CHF 52 (~$58) for the family; under-4s are not permitted for safety. Open early April–early November, ~9am–5pm in June.
spots.climate: Cliff-walled valley, ~2,600 ft. June is green and misty with frequent afternoon showers. Trümmelbach is inside the rock, so it is the smart rainy-morning pick; the open-valley waterfall walks want a drier window.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free Staubbach base walk and the village-to-Stechelberg valley path; pay only for Trümmelbach, which is genuinely unique.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the Wengen or Mürren cliff-shelf funicular for a car-free balcony village and a different angle on the valley.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurant Steinbeck — ~20 pizza varieties, kid-size portions available

  • Hotel Oberland — pizzas, pasta and soups with a garden in the village center

days.heading: Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe
days.feel: Highest railway in Europe, on the clearest morning

facts.label: Weather rule
facts.valueHtml: Go on the clearest forecast day; keep it flexible with First

days.note: The marquee splurge: cog rail to 3,454 m, the Aletsch Glacier, Ice Palace and Sphinx terrace. Near-freezing at the top even in June, and cloud can white it out — so this day floats to the best forecast morning of the block.

spots.name: Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe (3,454 m)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · jungfraujochIG · topofeuropeIG · aletschFlickr

images.alt: The Sphinx Observatory perched on the rock spire at the Jungfraujoch
The Aletsch Glacier sweeping between peaks from the Top of Europe
Visitors on the snow saddle at the Jungfraujoch under a sunstar sky

spots.cost: The single biggest line item of the whole leg. Plan off the Grindelwald round-trip fare (~CHF 239 adult in summer), with kids 6–15 at about CHF 20–30 (or free with a Swiss Family / Junior card), plus the CHF 10/person May–Oct reservation. Realistic family total: roughly CHF 560–580 (~$630–650). A Swiss Travel Pass gives only 25% off the summit railway — it is not included. Re-verify at jungfraujochtickets.ch before booking; peak fares run dynamic.
spots.climate: 3,454 m / near-freezing year-round. Expect roughly 28–36°F at the top even in June, regardless of valley heat — hats, gloves and real jackets. Cloud can white out the Aletsch view entirely, so keep a flex day and go on the clearest morning.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy the Grindelwald-side ticket (cheaper than Interlaken Ost), get free Junior/Family cards at any SBB station first, and pack summit snacks — the Crystal/Panorama self-service is pricey cafeteria fare.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The full summit experience — Ice Palace, Sphinx terrace, and a snow-play hour — is the once-in-a-lifetime payoff on a clear day; go all-in when the forecast is good.
spots.restoHtml:
• Crystal / Panorama self-service (summit) — fries, pasta, sandwiches; functional, not cheap
  • Bollywood restaurant (summit) — Indian, the novelty option at the top station
  • Pack lunch — the smartest move; eat a proper dinner back down in Grindelwald or the valley
spots.altboxHtml:
• Go on the clearest forecast day — this is why the Swiss block keeps a flex morning.
  • Schynige Platte or Männlichen as the lower-altitude big-view fallback if the summit is clouded.
  • Skip entirely and bank the ~$640 toward the Crete leg if weather never cooperates.

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: First Cliff Walk + First Flyer / Mountain Cart

facts.label: Kid win
facts.valueHtml: The single best day for the 8-year-old

days.note: The kid-magnet day: the cantilevered First Cliff Walk against the Eiger, then the First Flyer zipline, First Glider and Mountain Carts back down. Swap with Jungfraujoch if today’s summit forecast is the better one.

spots.name: Grindelwald-First: Cliff Walk + adventure day
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · grindelwaldfirstIG · firstcliffwalkIG · firstflyerFlickr

images.alt: The First Cliff Walk on the cliff edge below the glaciated Schreckhorn
Summer peaks and clouds doubled in the Bachalpsee reflection
The First Cliff Walk ducking under a rock overhang toward the Eiger

spots.cost: The single best kid-magnet of the leg. Gondola round-trip runs about CHF 76 adult in peak June (kids reduced; STP/Half-Fare ~50% off). The Cliff Walk is free with any gondola ticket. Add-on rides — First Flyer zipline, First Glider, Mountain Cart, Trottibike — start ~CHF 21 each; an Adventure Package bundling gondola + activities is ~CHF 69–99/person. A full family adventure day lands around CHF 500–600 (~$570–680).
spots.climate: 2,168 m. June is roughly 50–59°F up top, windier than the valley, with the usual Alpine afternoon-thunderstorm risk. Ride up in the morning, do the cliff walk and rides before clouds build, and keep rain shells in the pack.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy the gondola + one activity each rather than the whole ride menu; the Cliff Walk and Bachalpsee hike are free once you’re up.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Let each kid pick a First Flyer/Mountain Cart combo — this is the day the 8-year-old remembers most.
spots.restoHtml:
• Berggasthaus First (top station) — burgers, bacon-cheese penne, rösti, goulash soup, vegan options, big terrace
  • Grindelwald village pizzerias — plenty of plain-pizza/pasta fallbacks after the descent
  • Pack trail snacks — for the Bachalpsee walk if you extend the day
spots.altboxHtml:
• Bachalpsee hike (from First) — ~1 hr each way to the region’s iconic reflection lake.
  • Cliff Walk only if the kids just want the headline photo and the rides look too much.
  • Move to a clear day — swap with Jungfraujoch if the summit forecast is better today.

days.heading: Männlichen panorama + Lake Brienz
days.feel: Easy ridge view, then turquoise lake

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Männlichen Royal Walk — easy Eiger-Mönch-Jungfrau view

days.note: A gentler alpine day: the short Männlichen Royal Walk for the three-peak panorama, then glacier-turquoise Lake Brienz and the Iseltwald pier.

spots.name: Männlichen Royal Walk — easy Eiger–Mönch–Jungfrau panorama
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · mannlichenIG · royalwalkIG · grindelwaldFlickr

images.alt: The Eiger north face from the Männlichen ridge trail under blue sky
Cloud wrapping the Eiger above green Männlichen meadows
The Männlichen gondola descending toward the Lauterbrunnen valley

spots.cost: The best value big-view of the leg. Männlichen gondola from Grindelwald Terminal is about CHF 34 adult / ~CHF 17 child return — roughly half the Schynige Platte cog railway (CHF 68 adult). The Royal Walk itself (~2 km, +120 m, ~30 min to the crown platform) is free and genuinely stroller-and-8-year-old friendly.
spots.climate: ~2,230 m ridge. Cooler and breezier than the valley; the payoff is a dead-ahead Eiger–Mönch–Jungfrau wall from an easy, short walk. A good half-day to pair with the Lake Brienz afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride from the Grindelwald side (cheaper), do the free Royal Walk, and picnic at the top instead of buying summit food.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Walk the panorama ridge trail toward Kleine Scheidegg for a longer high balcony if the 13-year-old wants more.
spots.restoHtml:
• Berghaus Männlichen (top) — rösti and simple mountain plates at the crown
  • Grindelwald village — return for pizza/pasta and burgers after the ride down
  • Pack a summit picnic — cheapest and best-timed with the panorama
spots.altboxHtml:
• Schynige Platte instead if you’re Interlaken-side and want the alpine botanical garden.
  • Kleine Scheidegg ridge walk to extend the panorama for stronger legs.
  • Straight to Lake Brienz if clouds swallow the peaks — save the ridge for a clear slot.

spots.name: Lake Brienz: Iseltwald pier + Giessbach Falls boat
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lakebrienzIG · iseltwaldIG · giessbachFlickr

images.alt: The famous wooden Iseltwald pier reaching into turquoise Lake Brienz
The decorated MS Brienz cruising the turquoise water of Lake Brienz
A sailboat on Lake Brienz at sunset with warm reflections

spots.cost: The turquoise-lake day. A BLS lake boat runs its full schedule from late May; a one-way Interlaken Ost–Brienz seat is ~CHF 39 adult (kids reduced; free with pass). The famous Iseltwald wooden pier now has a turnstile with a ~CHF 5 entry to control crowds. The Giessbach funicular is likely bundled into a BLS combo ticket — confirm that fare before counting on it.
spots.climate: Glacier-fed, ~57–64°F in June. The vivid turquoise comes from glacial rock flour — but this is a look-don’t-swim lake in June; kids can wade, full swimming waits for the Crete leg. Official swim season is really July–August.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free Iseltwald village lanes and the short lakeshore, ride one boat leg rather than the full loop, and let the swimming happen in Crete.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The full Brienz → Giessbach → Iseltwald boat loop with the historic Giessbach funicular is a lovely slow half-day if the weather is calm.
spots.restoHtml:
• Chälet du Lac (Iseltwald) — explicit kids’ menu and portions, lake-fish specialties
  • Restaurant Seegarten (Iseltwald) — pizza, salads, burgers on a lakeside terrace
  • Strandhotel Iseltwald — lake-caught fish plus house plates on the water
spots.altboxHtml:
• Giessbach Falls funicular + terrace for the grand-hotel waterfall setting.
  • Brienz village woodcarving shops for a rainy-afternoon town stop.
  • Lake Thun / Spiez as the alternate turquoise-lake option from Interlaken’s west side.

days.heading: Chania old town and town beaches
days.daycost: Est. $160-$280 - beach snacks, parking/taxi, casual dinner
days.note: Do not rush to the far west on the first full Crete day. After four hiking days and two flight days, this easy 73-degree swim day is what makes the whole two-island structure feel worth it.

spots.name: Chania old town + Nea Chora / Agii Apostoli

spots.cost: Harbor wandering and town beaches are free. Add $60-$150 family for chairs, gelato, simple dinner, and taxis/parking depending where you stay.
spots.climate: June: Chania averages around 84 F highs / 66 F lows; sea water around 73 F is the payoff the whole route is built around.
spots.saveHtml: Save Make arrival and recovery days mostly free: harbor, beach, bakery breakfast, and a simple pizza/gyro dinner.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Use one harbor dinner or sunset boat if the flight day went smoothly; skip if the family just needs sleep.

days.heading: Balos boat from Kissamos

facts.label: Wind swap
facts.valueHtml: Trade days with Elafonissi if needed

days.heading: Imbros Gorge and south-coast swim
days.daycost: Est. $170-$330 - entrance, return ride/taxi, meals, fuel

facts.label: Hike
facts.valueHtml: 8km Imbros village -> Komitades; easier than Samaria

days.note: Imbros stays the family-accessible gorge: shorter, shadier, no ferry, and a good gut-check before deciding whether Samaria is a full descent or lazy-way outing on a later hiking day.

spots.name: Imbros Gorge + south-coast swim
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ImbrosFlickr

images.alt: A hiker spanning the towering walls at the narrowest point of Imbros Gorge
Golden light in the tight rock passage of Imbros Gorge
Sheer canyon walls and greenery along the Imbros Gorge trail

spots.cost: Entrance is typically EUR 3-EUR 5 pp cash. If self-driving, start at Imbros village and arrange a Komitades-to-Imbros return taxi/minibus before you begin; shared rides are commonly about EUR 8 pp, or roughly EUR 25-35 for a small private taxi.
spots.climate: 8 km, 2.5-4 hrs: easier and shorter than Samaria, mostly downhill from Imbros village to Komitades with shade in the narrows. Still rocky underfoot, with no services inside the gorge; start early and carry water.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the self-drive pattern: park at Imbros, walk down to Komitades, then take the pre-arranged local taxi/minibus back to the car. No ferry is required, which is why this is the gentler family gorge.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a Chania transfer tour if you do not want to manage the car-return logistics; the hike itself stays the same but the day becomes simpler.
spots.restoHtml:
• Oregano's — Agii Apostoli wood-fired pizza, fresh pasta, grilled meats, and Greek basics
  • Goody's Burger House — burgers, chicken burgers, fries, and junior menu fallback
  • Lithos Restaurant — beef burger with fries, grilled chicken, chicken/pork gyros, and skewers
spots.altboxHtml:
• Samaria Gorge ↩ — the epic 16 km version if everyone is trail-tested and the heat forecast cooperates.
  • Frangokastello Beach ↗ — south-coast swim and castle views after the gorge or as a low-effort swap.
  • Limnoupolis Water Park ↗ — straight kid-win backup for heat, wind, or hike fatigue.
