days.heading: Samaria Gorge: full White Mountains descent

facts.label: Logistics
facts.valueHtml: Early KTEL from Chania; ANENDYK ferry out; return bus from Sougia/Sfakia

days.note: Samaria supplies a full mountain-to-sea day when the family wants the leg’s biggest hike. For the 8-year-old, the complete descent is conditional; the shorter route from Agia Roumeli toward the Iron Gates is the kid-friendlier substitute.

spots.name: Samaria Gorge — full Lefka Ori descent
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Samaria GorgeIG · Lefka OriFlickr

images.alt: The footbridge at the Iron Gates where Samaria Gorge pinches between towering walls
Tiny hikers dwarfed by the narrowest squeeze of the Samaria Gorge walls
The cypress-lined switchback descent into Samaria Gorge from Xyloskalo

spots.cost: Plan roughly EUR 65-EUR 100 family for park entry, KTEL buses, and ANENDYK ferry tickets if self-guided; guided transfers commonly price higher but simplify the bus/ferry chain. Bring cash for small add-ons in Agia Roumeli.
spots.climate: Mountain start, hot finish: Xyloskalo/Omalos starts around 1,200-1,250 m, but the lower gorge and Agia Roumeli can feel full-summer hot by afternoon. Start on the first practical Chania bus, carry 2L+ water per adult, hats, snacks, and real shoes.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use public logistics if everyone is comfortable with the sequence: early KTEL Chania -> Xyloskalo/Omalos, hike to Agia Roumeli, ANENDYK ferry to Sougia or Chora Sfakion, then the waiting KTEL bus back to Chania.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a guided transfer day if you want one throat to choke for ferry timing, bus seats, and pickup. It does not make the 16 km easier; it only removes logistics friction.
spots.restoHtml:
• Xyloskalo Restaurant — trailhead breakfast/coffee with the gorge view before the descent.
  • Faragi, Agia Roumeli — post-hike taverna; fries, grilled meat, simple pasta/rice-style kid orders.
  • Goody's Burger House Chania — late, plain burger/fries fallback after the long return.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lazy way from Agia Roumeli ↩ — ferry to Agia Roumeli, walk about an hour / ~2 km up to the Iron Gates, then return to the beach and ferry. This is the kid-friendly Samaria version if the full descent is too much.
  • Agia Roumeli beach ↗ — if you finish early, swim/eat before the 17:30 ferry window.
  • Limnoupolis Water Park ↗ — the no-guilt bailout if heat, legs, or ferry logistics are wrong.

days.heading: Arrive Zurich, train to the Berner Oberland

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Check-in, Höheweg walk, groceries, early night

days.note: No Swiss rental car — the rail network reaches every mountain in this plan. Land, take the scenic train down, and let jet-lagged legs recover before the summit days.

spots.name: Interlaken soft landing: Höheweg + Harder Kulm view
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · interlakenIG · harderkulmIG · berneroberlandFlickr

images.alt: The Harder Kulm platform cantilevered above Interlaken between Lakes Thun and Brienz
Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau under a towering cumulus above Interlaken
Crepuscular sun rays breaking over Lake Thun and the Niesen pyramid

spots.cost: The Höheweg promenade and lakefronts are free. The Harder Kulm funicular is the paid add-on, but its published fare is genuinely inconsistent across sources (roughly CHF 19–51 adult depending on window/pass) — treat it as unknown until you check jungfrau.ch the week you travel. Half-Fare/Swiss Travel Pass takes ~50% off.
spots.climate: Valley floor, ~1,900 ft. June highs about 63°F / lows 47°F, with a high day-to-day rain probability (~57% chance of some rain). A relaxed arrival day is the right use of jet-lagged legs before the mountain days.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk the Höheweg, watch the paragliders land, and skip the funicular on arrival day; save Harder Kulm for a clear evening later in the block.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A clear-evening Harder Kulm sunset ride for the classic squeezed-between-two-lakes shot, if the sky cooperates.
spots.restoHtml:
• Luna Piccante (Wilderswil, ~6 min) — wood-fired pizza with a kids’ play area and free parking
  • Asllanis Corner — gourmet burgers and fries, casual and family-friendly
  • Ristorante e Pizzeria Sapori — classic Italian in the center, reliable picky-kid pizza/pasta
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lake Thun boat for a low-effort first afternoon if energy is very low.
  • Bönigen lakeshore for a quiet turquoise-water stroll away from the crowds.
  • Grocery + early night — the honest jet-lag choice before Jungfraujoch.

days.heading: Lauterbrunnen valley

facts.label: Weather rule
facts.valueHtml: Trümmelbach is inside the rock — the smart rainy-morning pick

days.note: The classic cliff-walled valley: 72 waterfalls, the Staubbach free-fall, and the Trümmelbach glacier torrents carved inside the mountain. Weather-flexible on purpose.

spots.name: Lauterbrunnen valley: 72 waterfalls + Trümmelbach
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lauterbrunnenIG · staubbachIG · trummelbachFlickr

images.alt: Lauterbrunnen valley at dusk with a silky river and snow peaks between the cliffs
The Lauterbrunnen valley sweeping toward the Jungfrau from the Wengen side
Traditional chalets under a towering cloud in the Lauterbrunnen valley

spots.cost: Staubbach Falls is free from the village. Trümmelbach Falls (the glacier torrents inside the mountain) charges about CHF 18 adult / CHF 8 child 6–15 — roughly CHF 52 (~$58) for the family; under-4s are not permitted for safety. Open early April–early November, ~9am–5pm in June.
spots.climate: Cliff-walled valley, ~2,600 ft. June is green and misty with frequent afternoon showers. Trümmelbach is inside the rock, so it is the smart rainy-morning pick; the open-valley waterfall walks want a drier window.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free Staubbach base walk and the village-to-Stechelberg valley path; pay only for Trümmelbach, which is genuinely unique.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the Wengen or Mürren cliff-shelf funicular for a car-free balcony village and a different angle on the valley.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurant Steinbeck — ~20 pizza varieties, kid-size portions available
  • Restaurant Weidstübli — pizza/pasta with vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options, Staubbach views
  • Hotel Oberland — pizzas, pasta and soups with a garden in the village center
spots.altboxHtml:
• Mürren (car-free shelf village) for the balcony view if the valley floor is socked in.
  • Trümmelbach only as a rainy-morning anchor, then regroup.
  • Wengen for an easy cog-rail town day with Jungfrau views.

days.heading: Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe
days.feel: Highest railway in Europe, on the clearest morning

facts.label: Weather rule
facts.valueHtml: Go on the clearest forecast day; keep it flexible with First

days.note: The marquee splurge: cog rail to 3,454 m, the Aletsch Glacier, Ice Palace and Sphinx terrace. Near-freezing at the top even in June, and cloud can white it out — so this day floats to the best forecast morning of the block.

spots.name: Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe (3,454 m)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · jungfraujochIG · topofeuropeIG · aletschFlickr

images.alt: The Sphinx Observatory perched on the rock spire at the Jungfraujoch
The Aletsch Glacier sweeping between peaks from the Top of Europe
Visitors on the snow saddle at the Jungfraujoch under a sunstar sky

spots.cost: The single biggest line item of the whole leg. Plan off the Grindelwald round-trip fare (~CHF 239 adult in summer), with kids 6–15 at about CHF 20–30 (or free with a Swiss Family / Junior card), plus the CHF 10/person May–Oct reservation. Realistic family total: roughly CHF 560–580 (~$630–650). A Swiss Travel Pass gives only 25% off the summit railway — it is not included. Re-verify at jungfraujochtickets.ch before booking; peak fares run dynamic.
spots.climate: 3,454 m / near-freezing year-round. Expect roughly 28–36°F at the top even in June, regardless of valley heat — hats, gloves and real jackets. Cloud can white out the Aletsch view entirely, so keep a flex day and go on the clearest morning.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy the Grindelwald-side ticket (cheaper than Interlaken Ost), get free Junior/Family cards at any SBB station first, and pack summit snacks — the Crystal/Panorama self-service is pricey cafeteria fare.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The full summit experience — Ice Palace, Sphinx terrace, and a snow-play hour — is the once-in-a-lifetime payoff on a clear day; go all-in when the forecast is good.
spots.restoHtml:
• Crystal / Panorama self-service (summit) — fries, pasta, sandwiches; functional, not cheap
  • Bollywood restaurant (summit) — Indian, the novelty option at the top station
  • Pack lunch — the smartest move; eat a proper dinner back down in Grindelwald or the valley
spots.altboxHtml:
• Go on the clearest forecast day — this is why the Swiss block keeps a flex morning.
  • Schynige Platte or Männlichen as the lower-altitude big-view fallback if the summit is clouded.
  • Skip entirely and bank the ~$640 toward the Crete leg if weather never cooperates.

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: First Cliff Walk + First Flyer / Mountain Cart

facts.label: Kid win
facts.valueHtml: The single best day for the 8-year-old

Summer peaks and clouds doubled in the Bachalpsee reflection

spots.cost: The single best kid-magnet of the leg. Gondola round-trip runs about CHF 76 adult in peak June (kids reduced; STP/Half-Fare ~50% off). The Cliff Walk is free with any gondola ticket. spots.saveHtml: Save Buy the gondola + one activity each rather than the whole ride menu; the Cliff Walk and Bachalpsee hike are free once you’re up.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Let each kid pick a First Flyer/Mountain Cart combo — this is the day the 8-year-old remembers most.

facts.label: Plan

days.note: No Swiss rental car — the rail network reaches every mountain in this plan. Land, take the scenic train down, and let jet-lagged legs recover before the summit days.

spots.name: Interlaken soft landing: Höheweg + Harder Kulm view
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · interlakenIG · harderkulmIG · berneroberlandFlickr

images.alt: The Harder Kulm platform cantilevered above Interlaken between Lakes Thun and Brienz
Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau under a towering cumulus above Interlaken

spots.cost: The Höheweg promenade and lakefronts are free. The Harder Kulm funicular is the paid add-on, but its published fare is genuinely inconsistent across sources (roughly CHF 19–51 adult depending on window/pass) — treat it as unknown until you check jungfrau.ch the week you travel. Half-Fare/Swiss Travel Pass takes ~50% off.
spots.climate: Valley floor, ~1,900 ft. June highs about 63°F / lows 47°F, with a high day-to-day rain probability (~57% chance of some rain). A relaxed arrival day is the right use of jet-lagged legs before the mountain days.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk the Höheweg, watch the paragliders land, and skip the funicular on arrival day; save Harder Kulm for a clear evening later in the block.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A clear-evening Harder Kulm sunset ride for the classic squeezed-between-two-lakes shot, if the sky cooperates.
spots.restoHtml:
• Luna Piccante (Wilderswil, ~6 min) — wood-fired pizza with a kids’ play area and free parking
  • Asllanis Corner — gourmet burgers and fries, casual and family-friendly
  • Ristorante e Pizzeria Sapori — classic Italian in the center, reliable picky-kid pizza/pasta
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lake Thun boat for a low-effort first afternoon if energy is very low.
  • Bönigen lakeshore for a quiet turquoise-water stroll away from the crowds.
  • Grocery + early night — the honest jet-lag choice before Jungfraujoch.

days.heading: Lauterbrunnen valley

facts.label: Weather rule
facts.valueHtml: Trümmelbach is inside the rock — the smart rainy-morning pick

days.note: The classic cliff-walled valley: 72 waterfalls, the Staubbach free-fall, and the Trümmelbach glacier torrents carved inside the mountain. Weather-flexible on purpose.

spots.name: Lauterbrunnen valley: 72 waterfalls + Trümmelbach
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lauterbrunnenIG · staubbachIG · trummelbachFlickr

images.alt: Lauterbrunnen valley at dusk with a silky river and snow peaks between the cliffs
The Lauterbrunnen valley sweeping toward the Jungfrau from the Wengen side
Traditional chalets under a towering cloud in the Lauterbrunnen valley

spots.cost: Staubbach Falls is free from the village. Trümmelbach Falls (the glacier torrents inside the mountain) charges about CHF 18 adult / CHF 8 child 6–15 — roughly CHF 52 (~$58) for the family; under-4s are not permitted for safety. Open early April–early November, ~9am–5pm in June.
spots.climate: Cliff-walled valley, ~2,600 ft. June is green and misty with frequent afternoon showers. Trümmelbach is inside the rock, so it is the smart rainy-morning pick; the open-valley waterfall walks want a drier window.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the free Staubbach base walk and the village-to-Stechelberg valley path; pay only for Trümmelbach, which is genuinely unique.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the Wengen or Mürren cliff-shelf funicular for a car-free balcony village and a different angle on the valley.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurant Steinbeck — ~20 pizza varieties, kid-size portions available
  • Restaurant Weidstübli — pizza/pasta with vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options, Staubbach views
  • Hotel Oberland — pizzas, pasta and soups with a garden in the village center
spots.altboxHtml:
• Mürren (car-free shelf village) for the balcony view if the valley floor is socked in.
  • Trümmelbach only as a rainy-morning anchor, then regroup.
  • Wengen for an easy cog-rail town day with Jungfrau views.

days.heading: Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe
days.feel: Highest railway in Europe, on the clearest morning

facts.label: Weather rule
facts.valueHtml: Go on the clearest forecast day; keep it flexible with First

days.note: The marquee splurge: cog rail to 3,454 m, the Aletsch Glacier, Ice Palace and Sphinx terrace. Near-freezing at the top even in June, and cloud can white it out — so this day floats to the best forecast morning of the block.

spots.name: Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe (3,454 m)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · jungfraujochIG · topofeuropeIG · aletschFlickr

images.alt: The Sphinx Observatory perched on the rock spire at the Jungfraujoch
The Aletsch Glacier sweeping between peaks from the Top of Europe
Visitors on the snow saddle at the Jungfraujoch under a sunstar sky

spots.cost: The single biggest line item of the whole leg. Plan off the Grindelwald round-trip fare (~CHF 239 adult in summer), with kids 6–15 at about CHF 20–30 (or free with a Swiss Family / Junior card), plus the CHF 10/person May–Oct reservation. Realistic family total: roughly CHF 560–580 (~$630–650). A Swiss Travel Pass gives only 25% off the summit railway — it is not included. Re-verify at jungfraujochtickets.ch before booking; peak fares run dynamic.
spots.climate: 3,454 m / near-freezing year-round. Expect roughly 28–36°F at the top even in June, regardless of valley heat — hats, gloves and real jackets. Cloud can white out the Aletsch view entirely, so keep a flex day and go on the clearest morning.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy the Grindelwald-side ticket (cheaper than Interlaken Ost), get free Junior/Family cards at any SBB station first, and pack summit snacks — the Crystal/Panorama self-service is pricey cafeteria fare.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The full summit experience — Ice Palace, Sphinx terrace, and a snow-play hour — is the once-in-a-lifetime payoff on a clear day; go all-in when the forecast is good.
spots.restoHtml:
• Crystal / Panorama self-service (summit) — fries, pasta, sandwiches; functional, not cheap
  • Bollywood restaurant (summit) — Indian, the novelty option at the top station
  • Pack lunch — the smartest move; eat a proper dinner back down in Grindelwald or the valley
spots.altboxHtml:
• Go on the clearest forecast day — this is why the Swiss block keeps a flex morning.
  • Schynige Platte or Männlichen as the lower-altitude big-view fallback if the summit is clouded.
  • Skip entirely and bank the ~$640 toward the Crete leg if weather never cooperates.

days.heading: Grindelwald-First adventure day

facts.label: Anchor
facts.valueHtml: First Cliff Walk + First Flyer / Mountain Cart

facts.label: Kid win
facts.valueHtml: The single best day for the 8-year-old

days.note: The kid-magnet day: the cantilevered First Cliff Walk against the Eiger, then the First Flyer zipline, First Glider and Mountain Carts back down. Swap with Jungfraujoch if today’s summit forecast is the better one.

spots.name: Grindelwald-First: Cliff Walk + adventure day
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · grindelwaldfirstIG · firstcliffwalkIG · firstflyerFlickr

images.alt: The First Cliff Walk on the cliff edge below the glaciated Schreckhorn
Summer peaks and clouds doubled in the Bachalpsee reflection
The First Cliff Walk ducking under a rock overhang toward the Eiger

spots.cost: The single best kid-magnet of the leg. Gondola round-trip runs about CHF 76 adult in peak June (kids reduced; STP/Half-Fare ~50% off). The Cliff Walk is free with any gondola ticket. Add-on rides — First Flyer zipline, First Glider, Mountain Cart, Trottibike — start ~CHF 21 each; an Adventure Package bundling gondola + activities is ~CHF 69–99/person. A full family adventure day lands around CHF 500–600 (~$570–680).
spots.climate: 2,168 m. June is roughly 50–59°F up top, windier than the valley, with the usual Alpine afternoon-thunderstorm risk. Ride up in the morning, do the cliff walk and rides before clouds build, and keep rain shells in the pack.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy the gondola + one activity each rather than the whole ride menu; the Cliff Walk and Bachalpsee hike are free once you’re up.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Let each kid pick a First Flyer/Mountain Cart combo — this is the day the 8-year-old remembers most.
spots.restoHtml:
• Berggasthaus First (top station) — burgers, bacon-cheese penne, rösti, goulash soup, vegan options, big terrace
  • Grindelwald village pizzerias — plenty of plain-pizza/pasta fallbacks after the descent
  • Pack trail snacks — for the Bachalpsee walk if you extend the day
spots.altboxHtml:
• Bachalpsee hike (from First) — ~1 hr each way to the region’s iconic reflection lake.
  • Cliff Walk only if the kids just want the headline photo and the rides look too much.
  • Move to a clear day — swap with Jungfraujoch if the summit forecast is better today.

days.heading: Männlichen panorama + Lake Brienz
days.feel: Easy ridge view, then turquoise lake

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Männlichen Royal Walk — easy Eiger-Mönch-Jungfrau view

days.note: A gentler alpine day: the short Männlichen Royal Walk for the three-peak panorama, then glacier-turquoise Lake Brienz and the Iseltwald pier.

spots.name: Männlichen Royal Walk — easy Eiger–Mönch–Jungfrau panorama
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · mannlichenIG · royalwalkIG · grindelwaldFlickr

images.alt: The Eiger north face from the Männlichen ridge trail under blue sky
Cloud wrapping the Eiger above green Männlichen meadows
The Männlichen gondola descending toward the Lauterbrunnen valley

spots.cost: The best value big-view of the leg. Männlichen gondola from Grindelwald Terminal is about CHF 34 adult / ~CHF 17 child return — roughly half the Schynige Platte cog railway (CHF 68 adult). The Royal Walk itself (~2 km, +120 m, ~30 min to the crown platform) is free and genuinely stroller-and-8-year-old friendly.
spots.climate: ~2,230 m ridge. Cooler and breezier than the valley; the payoff is a dead-ahead Eiger–Mönch–Jungfrau wall from an easy, short walk. A good half-day to pair with the Lake Brienz afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride from the Grindelwald side (cheaper), do the free Royal Walk, and picnic at the top instead of buying summit food.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Walk the panorama ridge trail toward Kleine Scheidegg for a longer high balcony if the 13-year-old wants more.
spots.restoHtml:
• Berghaus Männlichen (top) — rösti and simple mountain plates at the crown
  • Grindelwald village — return for pizza/pasta and burgers after the ride down
  • Pack a summit picnic — cheapest and best-timed with the panorama
spots.altboxHtml:
• Schynige Platte instead if you’re Interlaken-side and want the alpine botanical garden.
  • Kleine Scheidegg ridge walk to extend the panorama for stronger legs.
  • Straight to Lake Brienz if clouds swallow the peaks — save the ridge for a clear slot.

The Lago di Braies boathouse beneath steep Dolomite walls.

  • Chalet snack counter — fries, sandwiches, simple pasta, the fast picky-eater lunch
  • Ristorante Lago di Braies — independent lakeside spot, confirm pizza on the day’s menu
spots.altboxHtml:

days.heading: Tre Cime di Lavaredo — the big one

facts.label: Sleep
facts.valueHtml: San Vito di Cadore (Cortina) · night 3 of 5

days.note: The signature Dolomites day. The toll road drives you to 2,333m so the loop starts high — the 8-year-old walks under the three peaks without a summit push, the 13-year-old gets a real trail. Start early to beat the storms — and from the same Rifugio Auronzo car park you can bolt on the short Cadini di Misurina viewpoint at sunrise (see below).

spots.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · trecimeIG · dreizinnenIG · dolomitesFlickr

images.alt: The Tre Cime massif viewed from the loop trail
Tre Cime's classic three-tower profile under high alpine light
Tre Cime rising beyond the calm surface of Lake Misurina.

spots.cost: Toll road to Rifugio Auronzo €40/car (pre-book a timed slot at auronzo.info). Rifugio lunch ~€60–80/family.
spots.climate: 62°F day / 38°F night at 2,333m — afternoon storms are common; start the loop by 9am and be down by mid-afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the 7–9am toll slot for the best light and thinnest crowd, and pack sandwiches for the Locatelli viewpoint instead of a rifugio lunch (€15–18/plate × 4).
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Sleep at Rifugio Locatelli (~€60–70/person half-board) to get the blue-hour and sunrise faces without the day-trippers — bring cash, the huts don’t take cards.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rifugio Auronzo — self-service at the trailhead: pasta, wurstel, fries, polenta; easiest kid meal on the mountain
  • Rifugio Locatelli — the classic Three-Peaks view hut; plain polenta for picky eaters
  • Rifugio Lavaredo — trailside on the loop, same Alpine self-service and a good fallback if Locatelli is packed
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lago di Sorapis — a harder, quieter hike to a milky-turquoise lake (fixed cables) for the 13-year-old.
  • Monte Piana — a WWI open-air museum plateau above Lago di Misurina with trenches, tunnels, and 360° views.
  • Lago di Misurina lakeshore — the easy, flat option at the foot of the toll road if legs are done.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Tre Cime Loop Trail GuideThe Ultimate Tre Cime Guide (2026)

spots.name: Cadini di Misurina Viewpoint
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · cadinidimisurinaIG · dolomitesIG · misurinaFlickr

images.alt: Sunlit Cadini limestone spires rising above the trail
The Cadini promontory and its serrated limestone needles
Sunrise color washing the Cadini peaks.

spots.cost: No extra toll — same Rifugio Auronzo car park as Tre Cime (€40/car, one timed slot covers both). The viewpoint hike itself is free: ~3.9km out-and-back, ~1hr, only 144m of gain on path #117.
spots.climate: Easy hike, one exposed catch. Short and mostly gentle from the car park — but the famous photo promontory is a narrow ridge with cliff drop-offs. Doable with kids if you keep the 8-year-old close and stop short of the knife-edge tip; the 13-year-old is fine with care in dry weather. A right-side contour path skips the exposed crest entirely. Skip it if wet, icy, or windy.
spots.saveHtml: Save This is the rare free epic — no lift, no separate ticket. Do it first, at sunrise, before the Tre Cime loop while the light rakes the needles and the ridge is empty, then walk back to the car and start the big loop.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a local sunrise photo guide from Misurina — they know exactly where the family can stand safely for the postcard frame and handle the pre-dawn timing so you don't.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rifugio Auronzo — right at the trailhead; self-service pasta, wurstel, fries before or after the walk
  • Rifugio Col de Varda — the hut path #117 heads toward; chairlift-served, easy add for a strudel stop
  • Lakeside at Lago di Misurina — pizza and gelato by the lake at the foot of the toll road
spots.altboxHtml:
• Right-side contour path — the same viewpoint area without going over the exposed crest, if heights are a concern.
  • Lago di Misurina loop — a flat, stroller-easy lakeshore walk with a playground if the family skips the ridge.
  • Monte Piana — a WWI trench-and-tunnel plateau above the lake for a history-flavored alternative.
spots.bloglinksHtml: North Abroad — Best Dolomites Hikes & ViewpointsExactly How to Hike to the Cadini di Misurina Viewpoint

days.heading: Seceda’s ridge by cable car

facts.label: Sleep
facts.valueHtml: San Vito di Cadore (Cortina) · night 4 of 5

facts.label: Walk
facts.valueHtml: Ridge stroll, or hike down via Rifugio Firenze

days.note: The cable car does the climbing so everyone stands on the 2,500m Seceda ridge — the tilted-earth view of the Odle spires. Do the ridge walk before noon; willing hikers can ride up one-way and walk down to turn the ticket into the day’s trek.

spots.name: Seceda & Alpe di Siusi
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · secedaIG · alpedisiusiIG · valgardenaFlickr

images.alt: Seceda's knife-edge ridge and Odle spires
Seceda’s serrated ridge under sweeping alpine sky.
A dramatic Seceda panorama with cloud-wrapped spires.

spots.cost: Ortisei–Seceda cableway round trip ~€74 adult / €37 junior (8–15), under-8 free — ~€222/family. Timed-slot pre-booking required.
spots.climate: 57°F day / 38°F night on the 2,500m ridge — very exposed and windy; do the ridge walk before noon, before the storms build.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy one-way UP (€49 adult/€25 junior) and hike down via Rifugio Firenze — it turns the priciest ticket of the leg into the day’s epic hike and saves ~€25/adult.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The full Seceda–Rifugio Firenze–Baita Troier circuit with a mid-ridge rifugio lunch — a half-day alpine trek under the Odle spires with three hut stops.
spots.restoHtml:
• Baita Sanon — Alpe di Siusi, family-run Tyrolean/Ladin, explicitly kid-friendly, plain plates on request
  • Rifugio Firenze — on the ridge circuit; pasta, polenta, dumplings and an Odle-peaks terrace
  • Ristorante Bullaccia (Puflatsch) — Alpe di Siusi, fast-serving South Tyrolean for small kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Passo Giau — drive up the switchbacks to a wide-open meadow saddle with 360° views; no cable car, no timed slot.
  • Alpe di Siusi (Compatsch) — Europe’s largest alpine meadow, gentle and stroller-friendly by its own gondola.
  • Ortisei town — a pretty Val Gardena stroll if the ridge is socked in.

days.heading: Cinque Torri & Cortina — the lighter day

facts.label: Sleep
facts.valueHtml: San Vito di Cadore (Cortina) · night 5 of 5

days.note: Use the short Cinque Torri loop for a lighter alpine finale: WWI trenches beneath wild towers, then Cortina for a stroll and gelato.

spots.name: Cinque Torri
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · cinquetorriIG · dolomitesIG · cortinaFlickr

images.alt: Cinque Torri rising over an alpine meadow
Cinque Torri standing above the high alpine meadow.
Cinque Torri rising from a wide alpine plateau.

spots.cost: Chairlift return €27.50 adult (one-way €20.50); under-8 free, minors discounted — budget ~€75–85/family. 5% card discount in 2026.
spots.climate: 60°F day / 40°F night at Rifugio Scoiattoli (2,225m) — short and easy, so it forgives a late-morning start after a slow breakfast.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pay by credit card at the base for the built-in 5% discount, then walk the free ~2km WWI-trench loop once you’re up — one of the cheapest “epic scenery” stops of the whole trip.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the beginner via-ferrata-lite from Rifugio Scoiattoli toward Averau (short, guided) for the 13-year-old — a real climbing memory while the rest of the family relaxes on the terrace.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rifugio Scoiattoli — right under the towers; casunziei ravioli and polenta, flag ahead for a plain-pasta kid plate
  • Rifugio Averau — a 30-min walk on, sommelier-run homemade pasta; confirm a simple option
  • Rifugio Cinque Torri — casual at the base of the towers; casunziei, ricotta strudel, homemade bread
spots.altboxHtml:
• Rifugio Lagazuoi — a 5-minute cable car to a WWI tunnel network and a panoramic hut at Passo Falzarego.
  • Nuvolau / Averau loop — a longer scramble to a 360° summit view for the strong-legged.
  • Lago Ghedina — a quiet, forest-ringed little lake near Cortina for an easy afternoon.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Cinque Torri Hike & RifugiosCinque Torri with Kids

spots.name: Cortina d'Ampezzo & the Faloria Cable Car
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · cortinaIG · dolomitesIG · faloriaFlickr

images.alt: Aerial view of Cinque Torri and the Tofana wall above Cortina
The Tofane wall dominating the Cortina skyline.
A high Dolomite pass above the Cortina region.

spots.cost: Faloria cable car ~€27 adult / ~€20 under-16 (~€94/family). Freccia nel Cielo to Cima Tofana €45 adult round trip.
spots.climate: 65°F day / 45°F night in town (1,224m) — mornings are the reliably clear window; storms roll through most afternoons.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride Faloria (~half the price of Freccia nel Cielo) for a comparable panorama, and window-shop Corso Italia for free — the 2026-Olympics town is a stroll, not a ticket.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Freccia nel Cielo all the way to Cima Tofana (3,244m, €45 adult) — the single highest, most dramatic viewpoint reachable without technical climbing on the whole trip.
spots.restoHtml:
• Ristorante Pizzeria 5 Torri — Corso Italia, busy family standby, traditional pizza and pasta
  • Pizzeria Ai Due Forni — town center, pizza by the slice or whole, the fast post-hike dinner
  • El Camineto — above town with a valley view; polenta, grilled meats, simple pasta for kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lago di Sorapis viewpoint (Passo Tre Croci) — roadside massif views instead of a second cable car if legs are tired.
  • Rifugio Lagazuoi + WWI tunnels — a cable-car-and-history half day at Passo Falzarego.
  • Mercato / gelato on Corso Italia — a low-key town afternoon before the flight south.

spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A private 45-minute rowboat (€55) at golden hour for the postcard frame — wooden hull, the boathouse behind you, the peaks doubled in the water.
spots.restoHtml:
• Panorama (Hotel Lago di Braies) — lake-view terrace, South Tyrolean; simple pasta for kids, reserve ahead
  • Chalet snack counter — fries, sandwiches, simple pasta, the fast picky-eater lunch
  • Ristorante Lago di Braies — independent lakeside spot, confirm pizza on the day’s menu
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lago di Carezza — a zero-hike, drive-up alpine lake below the Latemar with no reservation system.
  • Lago di Dobbiaco — a flat, stroller-easy lake loop close to the base.
  • Prato Piazza (Plätzwiese) — a high meadow plateau if the family wants views without a climb.

days.heading: Tre Cime di Lavaredo — the big one

facts.label: Sleep
facts.valueHtml: San Vito di Cadore (Cortina) · night 3 of 5

days.note: The signature Dolomites day. The toll road drives you to 2,333m so the loop starts high — the 8-year-old walks under the three peaks without a summit push, the 13-year-old gets a real trail. Start early to beat the storms — and from the same Rifugio Auronzo car park you can bolt on the short Cadini di Misurina viewpoint at sunrise (see below).

spots.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · trecimeIG · dreizinnenIG · dolomitesFlickr

images.alt: The Tre Cime massif viewed from the loop trail
Tre Cime's classic three-tower profile under high alpine light
Tre Cime rising beyond the calm surface of Lake Misurina.

spots.cost: Toll road to Rifugio Auronzo €40/car (pre-book a timed slot at auronzo.info). Rifugio lunch ~€60–80/family.
spots.climate: 62°F day / 38°F night at 2,333m — afternoon storms are common; start the loop by 9am and be down by mid-afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the 7–9am toll slot for the best light and thinnest crowd, and pack sandwiches for the Locatelli viewpoint instead of a rifugio lunch (€15–18/plate × 4).
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Sleep at Rifugio Locatelli (~€60–70/person half-board) to get the blue-hour and sunrise faces without the day-trippers — bring cash, the huts don’t take cards.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rifugio Auronzo — self-service at the trailhead: pasta, wurstel, fries, polenta; easiest kid meal on the mountain
  • Rifugio Locatelli — the classic Three-Peaks view hut; plain polenta for picky eaters
  • Rifugio Lavaredo — trailside on the loop, same Alpine self-service and a good fallback if Locatelli is packed
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lago di Sorapis — a harder, quieter hike to a milky-turquoise lake (fixed cables) for the 13-year-old.
  • Monte Piana — a WWI open-air museum plateau above Lago di Misurina with trenches, tunnels, and 360° views.
  • Lago di Misurina lakeshore — the easy, flat option at the foot of the toll road if legs are done.

spots.name: Cadini di Misurina Viewpoint
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · cadinidimisurinaIG · dolomitesIG · misurinaFlickr

images.alt: Sunlit Cadini limestone spires rising above the trail
The Cadini promontory and its serrated limestone needles
Sunrise color washing the Cadini peaks.

spots.cost: No extra toll — same Rifugio Auronzo car park as Tre Cime (€40/car, one timed slot covers both). The viewpoint hike itself is free: ~3.9km out-and-back, ~1hr, only 144m of gain on path #117.
spots.climate: Easy hike, one exposed catch. Short and mostly gentle from the car park — but the famous photo promontory is a narrow ridge with cliff drop-offs. Doable with kids if you keep the 8-year-old close and stop short of the knife-edge tip; the 13-year-old is fine with care in dry weather. A right-side contour path skips the exposed crest entirely. Skip it if wet, icy, or windy.
spots.saveHtml: Save This is the rare free epic — no lift, no separate ticket. Do it first, at sunrise, before the Tre Cime loop while the light rakes the needles and the ridge is empty, then walk back to the car and start the big loop.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a local sunrise photo guide from Misurina — they know exactly where the family can stand safely for the postcard frame and handle the pre-dawn timing so you don't.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rifugio Auronzo — right at the trailhead; self-service pasta, wurstel, fries before or after the walk
  • Rifugio Col de Varda — the hut path #117 heads toward; chairlift-served, easy add for a strudel stop
  • Lakeside at Lago di Misurina — pizza and gelato by the lake at the foot of the toll road
spots.altboxHtml:
• Right-side contour path — the same viewpoint area without going over the exposed crest, if heights are a concern.
  • Lago di Misurina loop — a flat, stroller-easy lakeshore walk with a playground if the family skips the ridge.
  • Monte Piana — a WWI trench-and-tunnel plateau above the lake for a history-flavored alternative.

facts.label: Walk
facts.valueHtml: Ridge stroll, or hike down via Rifugio Firenze

days.note: The cable car does the climbing so everyone stands on the 2,500m Seceda ridge — the tilted-earth view of the Odle spires. Do the ridge walk before noon; willing hikers can ride up one-way and walk down to turn the ticket into the day’s trek.

spots.cost: Ortisei–Seceda cableway round trip ~€74 adult / €37 junior (8–15), under-8 free — ~€222/family. Timed-slot pre-booking required.
spots.climate: 57°F day / 38°F night on the 2,500m ridge — very exposed and windy; do the ridge walk before noon, before the storms build.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy one-way UP (€49 adult/€25 junior) and hike down via Rifugio Firenze — it turns the priciest ticket of the leg into the day’s epic hike and saves ~€25/adult.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The full Seceda–Rifugio Firenze–Baita Troier circuit with a mid-ridge rifugio lunch — a half-day alpine trek under the Odle spires with three hut stops.
spots.restoHtml:
• Baita Sanon — Alpe di Siusi, family-run Tyrolean/Ladin, explicitly kid-friendly, plain plates on request
  • Rifugio Firenze — on the ridge circuit; pasta, polenta, dumplings and an Odle-peaks terrace
  • Ristorante Bullaccia (Puflatsch) — Alpe di Siusi, fast-serving South Tyrolean for small kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Passo Giau — drive up the switchbacks to a wide-open meadow saddle with 360° views; no cable car, no timed slot.
  • Alpe di Siusi (Compatsch) — Europe’s largest alpine meadow, gentle and stroller-friendly by its own gondola.
  • Ortisei town — a pretty Val Gardena stroll if the ridge is socked in.

spots.cost: Chairlift return €27.50 adult (one-way €20.50); under-8 free, minors discounted — budget ~€75–85/family. 5% card discount in 2026.

spots.altboxHtml:

  • Nuvolau / Averau loop — a longer scramble to a 360° summit view for the strong-legged.
  • Lago Ghedina — a quiet, forest-ringed little lake near Cortina for an easy afternoon.

spots.cost: Faloria cable car ~€27 adult / ~€20 under-16 (~€94/family). Freccia nel Cielo to Cima Tofana €45 adult round trip.
spots.climate: 65°F day / 45°F night in town (1,224m) — mornings are the reliably clear window; storms roll through most afternoons.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride Faloria (~half the price of Freccia nel Cielo) for a comparable panorama, and window-shop Corso Italia for free — the 2026-Olympics town is a stroll, not a ticket.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Freccia nel Cielo all the way to Cima Tofana (3,244m, €45 adult) — the single highest, most dramatic viewpoint reachable without technical climbing on the whole trip.

spots.altboxHtml:

  • Rifugio Lagazuoi + WWI tunnels — a cable-car-and-history half day at Passo Falzarego.
  • Mercato / gelato on Corso Italia — a low-key town afternoon before the flight south.
